detail.abstract: This study investigated vote selling as an economic survival strategy among Nigerian voters, examining the extent to which poverty and food insecurity influence transactional voting during elections. Anchored on Rational Choice Theory and Political Clientelism Theory, the primary objective was to determine whether acute socioeconomic pressures drive voter participation in clientelist networks, while assessing public perceptions regarding its broader implications for democratic governance. A quantitative survey design was adopted, yielding a sample of 1,605 valid respondents analyzed through descriptive statistics, Cronbach's Alpha reliability testing, Pearson Product-Moment correlation, multiple linear regression, and subgroup variance tests (ANOVA and Independent Samples t-test).

title: Health as a Fundamental Right in Nepal: Legal Provisions and Implementation Gaps

detail.title: Health as a Fundamental Right in Nepal: Legal Provisions and Implementation Gaps
detail.abstract: The Constitution of Nepal, 2015, recognizes health as a fundamental right of all citizens. The Constitution, article 35 provides for the right to free basic health services, emergency health care and equal access to health services without discrimination. This constitutional commitment is a major legal achievement in the transformation of Nepal to a federal democratic republic. There remains, however, a wide gap between the legal provisions and their actual implementation. This paper is a case study of health as a basic right in Nepal. It discusses the legal framework, the institutional set up for health services and the persisting implementation gaps that deny millions of Nepali citizens their constitutional right to health. Drawing on publicly available data from the Ministry of Health and Population, World Health Organization, World Bank, Central Bureau of Statistics and other sources, the analysis shows that Nepal continues to grapple with serious health challenges, despite constitutional guaranties. Out-of-pocket health expenditure is high at about 55 percent of total health spending, pushing many households into poverty. Health infrastructure is unevenly distributed among provinces and local governments. The health budget has increased but remains below international levels. Maternal mortality is still high and non-communicable diseases are on the rise. The paper highlights some gaps in implementation like weak legal enforcement mechanisms, health financing, health workers, health infrastructure and governance, social discrimination and awareness of health rights. The case study also discusses specific examples of these gaps such as between urban and rural areas, difficulties in remote mountain districts, and the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. The paper concludes with recommendations on strengthening legal enforcement, scaling up health financing, enhancing capacity of health systems, promoting health equity and empowering citizens to claim their health rights. The findings have implications for Nepal's ongoing federal transition, as well as for other developing countries that have recognized health as a fundamental right, but have failed to realize this right in practice.

title: PhD Project: Mixed Markets, Mixed Enforcement? An Empirical Study of Competition Law Enforcement against State-owned Enterprises
affiliations: Utrecht University School of Law and

detail.title: PhD Project: Mixed Markets, Mixed Enforcement? An Empirical Study of Competition Law Enforcement against State-owned Enterprises

keywords: Mixed Enforcement? An Empirical Study of EU Competition Law Enforcement Against State-Owned Enterprises

detail.abstract:
State ownership has been rediscovered across the EU for industrial policy purposes, proving effective in the pursuit of strategic autonomy and sustainability transitions. State-owned enterprises (SOEs) are historically prominent in critical markets such as energy, extraction, utilities, finance and transportation, while allowing for more government influence than in private firms.

The above developments have led to a resurgence of state ownership through nationalization, active shareholding and subsidization in the EU, creating new risks for so-called mixed markets, where SOEs and private firms compete. This, in turn, raises questions about competition law enforcement of such markets. SOEs may be inclined to behave anticompetitively and create obstacles for private enterprises. However, there is little understanding of how competition law is enforced against SOEs in practice. This PhD research seeks to establish the first empirical insights into the practice and constraints of competition law enforcement against SOEs. 

• As PhD researcher, you will undertake a 4-year research project aimed at answering to what extent, and on what grounds, the enforcement of EU competition law differs between State-owned enterprises and private undertakings. 
• This PhD project envisions a mixed methods approach, combining data-driven, experimental and qualitative methodologies.
• The envisioned output of this PhD is 4 academic articles suitable for publication in peer-reviewed academic journals in competition law or policy.
• Throughout this project you will work in close collaboration with two dedicated PhD supervisors, who will coach you towards becoming an independent academic researcher.

detail.abstract: The activities of audit-oversight bodies, most notably audit committees in U.S. and U.K. firms, are central to the reliability of financial reporting. Evidence on them, however, rests largely on inputs and structural attributes (independence, expertise, meeting frequency, governance form), which capture the capacity for oversight and leave the substance of what these bodies do unobserved. We address this gap in Japan, where annual securities reports have been required since 2019 to describe those activities in narrative form. Applying a large language model (GPT-4o) to read that narrative in context, we construct an Audit Oversight Score (AOS) that grades reported oversight activity at scale, separating specific and evidenced activity from boilerplate instead of counting words, and split it into the body's own activity (ACT) and its coordination with the external auditor (COORD). The measure agrees with human coders as closely as two human coders agree with each other, and is reproduced by three other models. In an FY2019-FY2024 panel, substantive differences persist across firms and are not explained by the governance structure a firm has chosen. Firms scoring higher pay higher audit fees, consistent with oversight and the external audit being complements. During the COVID-19 pandemic, when incentives to misreport rose, a higher ACT is associated with smaller absolute discretionary accruals even within the same firm. Both associations run through ACT rather than COORD, an asymmetry visible only once oversight is measured along two dimensions.

title: Invariant Regimes in Boltzmann -Lotka -Volterra Dynamics

detail.title: Invariant Regimes in Boltzmann -Lotka -Volterra Dynamics
detail.abstract: Boltzmann-Lotka-Volterra (BLV) frameworks are widely used to model artificial complex systems such as urban dynamics, spatial economics, mobility, and contagion processes. Over several decades these models have undergone substantial refinement, incorporating richer algebraic structures, multiscale coupling, behavioral heterogeneity, and empirical calibration. Despite this increasing sophistication, recurrent qualitative features (including regime multiplicity, path dependence, tipping points, and strong sensitivity to initial conditions) persist across applications. This paper examines BLV-based models from a structural dynamical perspective. Fixing a canonical BLV formulation, we analyze how successive refinements modify functional expressions while preserving the underlying dynamical operator. We show that refinements that preserve entropy-normalized allocation, multiplicative Lotka-Volterra interaction structure, and state-space dimensionality leave the qualitative regime topology invariant. As a result, increasing model sophistication can improve descriptive resolution without expanding the space of dynamically admissible behaviors. This invariance leads to a phenomenon we term structural saturation, in which successive epistemological refinements stabilize and map regime boundaries without altering the qualitative structure of the dynamical system. The analysis clarifies the structural domain within which BLV frameworks operate and provides a criterion for  distinguishing productive refinement from situations where qualitative behavior cannot change without modifying the underlying operator. The results suggest that persistent qualitative features observed in BLV applications may reflect intrinsic properties of the operator rather than insufficient model refinement.

detail.abstract: Pakistan has developed an increasingly sophisticated formal architecture for responding to human trafficking-the Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act 2018, a National Action Plan (2021-2025), and an emerging National Database on Trafficking in Persons-yet outcomes remain almost uniformly poor: a national gender-based violence (GBV) conviction rate near 5%, and provincial data showing zero convictions across hundreds of rape and domestic-violence cases. This article synthesizes legal-doctrinal scholarship, institutional criminal-justice research, primary government and UN monitoring data, and journalistic incident data to ask how gendered institutional practice-rather than the adequacy of the law alone-shapes whether trafficking cases involving GBV are identified, evidenced, and progressed through Pakistan's criminal justice system. Drawing on Feminist Institutionalism and Street-Level Bureaucracy theory, the article traces an institutional attrition pathway from report to outcome, and shows that the single largest predictor of conviction is not the strength of evidence but which statute a case happens to be prosecuted under: cases routed through the Pakistan Penal Code achieve a 1.2% conviction rate, while functionally similar cases prosecuted under the PTPA achieve 37.8%. The article argues that this statutory-routing effect is itself a gendered institutional practice, shaped by frontline discretion operating under resource constraint, and identifies a concrete research and policy gap at the intersection of gendered victimization, evidence generation, and inter-agency coordination.

title: The Interior Cap: Partial Caps and the Residual Read

detail.title: The Interior Cap: Partial Caps and the Residual Read
detail.abstract: Emphasis regimes in audit reporting let the profession select which matters to examine closely, and standards name no number: reports carry a handful drawn from a much longer list. A companion paper showed that such regimes inform only because emphasis is scarce, but its cap was binary-one matter, or all of them. This paper opens the interval between, which two attributes cannot represent, and finds the cap worth more as a quantity than as a switch. One relation organises the results: the cap and the due-care defense are complements, rationing being worthless where courts credit nothing and decisive where they credit everything. At full credit a partial cap does not die. What survives has a closed form-the liability read collapses to α times the squared maximum over the uncovered coordinates, exactly, free of the instance, of the number of attributes, and of the cap itself-so amnesty requires either free coverage or weakest-link doctrine, the honest burden is exactly linear in the doctrine, and what stays legible about a profession is the image of the competence it declined to advertise. Free coverage, meanwhile, is never uniquely best at telling candid firms from evasive ones; where the best cap is unique it is always interior, and the interior cap also makes its labels more expensive to forge. Choosing what to emphasise turns out to be choosing which coordinate answers: a best pair need not contain the best single item, because a set can relocate the binding coordinate where a singleton can only shield it-an effect specific to doctrines that price the extremes of a capability profile, and absent wherever the whole profile is read. The design claim inverts the companion's exclusivity rule, under which a regime could credit generously or let senders file freely but not both: with an interior cap the two coexist, because the regime still prices what was left out. Rationing is what makes generosity affordable.

title: Emission reduction pathway optimization and comprehensive benefit assessment in the Pearl River Delta based on a deep learning response surface model
affiliations: Jinan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jinan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Emission reduction pathway optimization and comprehensive benefit assessment in the Pearl River Delta based on a deep learning response surface model
detail.abstract: Despite intensified mitigation efforts, ozone (O3) concentrations in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) remain volatile and prone to rebounding, posing persistent risks to public health and agricultural ecosystems. Using a 2023 baseline emission inventory and a 3% regional O3 reduction target grounded in recent volatility trends, this study constructed an optimization framework integrating a deep learning-based response surface model, a genetic algorithm, and marginal abatement cost curves to minimize total societal emission reduction costs. The optimal synergistic pathway requires average NOx and VOCs reductions of 18.9% and 20.0%, respectively, achieving a 3.6%-4.1% O3 decline at a total cost of 0.83 billion CNY, with a benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 7.6. BCRs varied substantially across cities, ranging from 1.3 to 35.0, underscoring the need for phased, city-differentiated emission reduction policies. This pathway can avoid 1,196 premature deaths during the 2023 warm season (95% UI: 582-1943) and significantly improve spatial and socioeconomic equity, indicated by a 10% decrease in the O3 exposure Gini coefficient and a 21.4% reduction in the absolute value of the health burden concentration index. In addition, the optimal pathway reduces O3-induced crop yield losses and avoids more than 20 million CNY in direct agricultural economic losses. This study provides a quantitative scientific basis for precise and coordinated O3 control in the PRD and offers a transferable technical approach for air quality management in other key regions of China.

detail.abstract: The global transition from traditional to sustainable finance has become increasingly urgent as climate change accelerates, regulatory pressure intensifies, and biodiversity loss threatens developing economies. Despite growing momentum in green finance, banking sector adoption remains fragmented, constrained by inconsistent regulatory frameworks, limited market transparency, and weak incentive structures, particularly in low and middle-income economies. Stock exchanges are increasingly positioned as pivotal intermediaries capable of bridging this gap, however, their specific role remains insufficiently examined. This study investigates how stock exchanges can promote green finance adoption by banks globally through mixed-methods analysis synthesising 64 sources and primary data collected from financial practitioners. Four interdependent drivers of adoption are identified: market regulations, market mechanisms, awareness, and incentives. Notably, data from the International Monetary Fund and the International Organization of Securities Commissions confirm that only 49% of regulators in low-income economies maintain supportive market regulations, compared with 85% in high-income OECD nations. These findings indicate that stock exchanges must transition from voluntary guidance to binding frameworks mandating Environmental, Social and Governance disclosure and green bond standards for listed banks, supported by targeted tax incentives, formalised peer exchange partnerships, and standardised disclosure in carbon markets to direct capital toward achieving net-zero by 2050.

title:
Mitigating the Pollution-climate Feedback Loop in a Polycrisis System: 
Macroeconomic, Thermodynamic, and Network-Systems Strategies for Breaking Re inforcing Environmental Cycles

detail.title:
Mitigating the Pollution-climate Feedback Loop in a Polycrisis System: 
Macroeconomic, Thermodynamic, and Network-Systems Strategies for Breaking Re inforcing Environmental Cycles
detail.abstract:
The report argues that modern environmental destabilization emerges from a tightly coupled Pollution‑Climate Feedback Loop operating inside a global polycrisis, where toxic pollutants, atmospheric thermodynamics, biophysical tipping cascades, and macro‑financial fragility reinforce one another. As the document states, “industrial pollution exacerbates climate disruption, and climate disruption in turn intensifies the toxicity… and economic burden of environmental pollutants” . Conventional climate models and policy frameworks fail because they treat CO₂, air pollution, and macroeconomic stability as separate domains, ignoring non‑linear amplification across atmospheric chemistry, boundary‑layer dynamics, wildfire aerosols, labor productivity, and sovereign debt markets.

The study synthesizes non‑equilibrium thermodynamics, multiplex network theory, and strategic macro‑finance to show how second‑law exergy destruction, aerosol masking, ozone‑driven vegetation dieback, and wildfire black‑carbon cascades create reinforcing loops that multiply damages far beyond standard IAM projections. As the report notes, “over 72% of all primary energy extracted is destroyed as unusable waste exergy… discharged as disordered, chemically reactive pollutants” . This thermodynamic inefficiency feeds boundary‑layer stagnation, urban heat traps, and atmospheric chemistry that intensifies warming.

To break these cycles, the report proposes a three‑pillar intervention architecture: (1) fast‑track abatement of short‑lived climate pollutants (SLCPs) to avoid aerosol‑termination warming shocks; (2) closed‑loop industrial exergy cascading and radiative sky cooling to reduce waste‑heat forcing; and (3) macro‑financial restructuring—including dual‑rate green refinancing and multilateral de‑risking—to compress emerging‑market WACC and unlock clean‑infrastructure investment. Coordinated implementation averts trillions in projected GDP losses and prevents the system from locking into high‑entropy, fossil‑dependent trajectories.

title: Green Gold: Avocado Production and Conflict in Mexico

detail.title: Green Gold: Avocado Production and Conflict in Mexico
detail.abstract: The surge in global demand for Mexican avocados, particularly from the United States, has led to increased production and revenue in avocado-producing municipalities of Mexico. I show that these external changes in avocado global consumption patterns have influenced conflict levels in Mexico. Combining geographical variations in avocado cultivation suitability and fluctuations in avocado demand over time, I find a notable rise in homicides among agricultural workers in municipalities that are well-suited for avocado production. I demonstrate that this rise in homicides is not explained by the increased presence of drug cartels but rather heightened competition between cartels for resources in municipalities where avocados are produced. These findings suggest that cartels vie for territorial control, diversifying their income sources, including the avocado industry, in response to their relatively limited influence over drug markets and routes.

title: Federated Big Data Processing in Multi-Cloud Architectures
affiliations: ,  Tata Consultancy Services, Unaffiliated Authors, Elevance Health, Inc. and Unaffiliated Authors

detail.title: Federated Big Data Processing in Multi-Cloud Architectures
detail.abstract: The accelerated pace of big data and the resulting spread of distributed applications have led to the requirement of scalable, secure, and efficient data processing platforms in the heterogeneous cloud environment. Federated big data processing on multi-clouds is a promising paradigm that can overcome the problems of data sovereignty, interoperability and performance optimization. This paper proposes a holistic view of how federated processing pipelines can be designed, which would allow multiple cloud service providers to collaborate seamlessly and maintain data locality, compliance, and resiliency. The suggested architecture uses the principles of containerization, orchestration, and federated learning to reduce communication overhead and streamline the use of resources across clouds. In addition, security-enhancing protocols like policy-driven access controls, differentiation privacy, and homomorphic encryption are incorporated to protect sensitive data when processing inter-clouds. Scalability, fault tolerance, query responsiveness, and other experimental results have been shown to greatly improve over traditional single-cloud solutions. The results indicate that federated multiclouds can provide the backbone to the next generation of big data applications in finance, healthcare, and smart cities, where data diversity, security, and compliance are of utmost importance.

title: The Indivisibility of Option Replication and Portfolio Theory: Uncovering the Mechanics of the Moore Option Pricing Model in the Second Loop
affiliations: University of Toledo

detail.title: The Indivisibility of Option Replication and Portfolio Theory: Uncovering the Mechanics of the Moore Option Pricing Model in the Second Loop

keywords: Financial Economics Working Paper Series JEL Classification: G12 (Asset Pricing)

detail.abstract: This paper provides an empirical and theoretical re-examination of options crosssectional pricing by demonstrating that the options surface can be systematically modeled as a log-linear weighted portfolio rate asset in the Moore Option Pricing Model. The model is a variable drift Fokker-Planck derived pricing model that solves the basic Black-Scholes model for the interest rate with a solved unity optimal variance. Rather than treating contingent claims as speculative black boxes requiring strike-specific variance parameters, our framework demonstrates that the contract cross-section is fully explained by a native, natural log-additive two-component vector field: an active leverage-constrained equity replication leg and a continuous probabilistic boundary funding constraint. Testing the matrix against the canonical January 2, 1990 S&P 500 Index options dataset yields outstanding empirical results. The model solves a single, perfectly uniform implied stock return parameter (21.01%) across the entire contract chain, establishing a strict, structure-preserving compositional isomorphism. Passing our extracted uniform drift field backward through the static replication weights reconstructs the entire sixteen-strike premium vector back to the penny, confirming that the no-intercept layout triggers a flawless bidirectional identity that handles microscopic market friction effortlessly, deflating transaction noise down to a minor 14-cent residual ripple per contract. This absolute cross-sectional coherence provides definitive proof that portfolio theory integrates flawlessly with this classic solution trace, resolving much of the multi-decade mystery of derivative pricing by dissolving the MacBeth-Merville (1979) spatial decay and the post-1987 volatility smile by identity.

title: Planetary Cooling Pathways: Scientific Scenarios for Returning to a Stable Climate State

detail.title: Planetary Cooling Pathways: Scientific Scenarios for Returning to a Stable Climate State
detail.abstract:
Humanity has entered a dangerous climate overshoot regime in which achieving net‑zero emissions is no longer sufficient to restore Earth system stability. As the report states, “net‑zero halts additional greenhouse gas radiative forcing, but it stabilizes global temperatures at an elevated, dangerous plateau” . Even with full decarbonization, ocean thermal inertia, cryosphere disintegration, and carbon cycle hysteresis lock in centuries of warming and tipping‑element activation.

This research develops a century‑scale scientific architecture for Planetary Cooling—the intentional reduction of global mean surface temperature back toward the Holocene stability envelope (<1.0 °C, ~350 ppm CO₂). The analysis integrates Earth’s Energy Imbalance dynamics, ocean heat persistence, carbon cycle hysteresis, and multi‑vector interventions across both longwave and shortwave radiative pathways.

The core conclusion is that meaningful cooling within 50–100 years requires a Two‑Pronged Planetary Architecture:

  1. Gigatonne‑Scale Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) delivering 15–22 Gt CO₂/yr by 2060–2080 through DACCS, Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement, Enhanced Rock Weathering, and biochar. This longwave restoration permanently reduces greenhouse forcing but operates on decadal–century timescales.

  2. Temporary Solar Radiation Modification (SRM)—specifically multi‑latitude Stratospheric Aerosol Injection or Marine Cloud Brightening—to “shave” 0.5–0.8 °C of peak warming and prevent irreversible tipping‑element collapse while CDR scales. As the report notes, “SAI must never be deployed without binding, scaled CDR deployment” due to termination‑shock risks .

The report outlines a four‑phase planetary cooling timeline (2026–2100), governance requirements under a UN Planetary Cooling Oversight Council, and macroeconomic valuation showing >3.5:1 benefit‑cost ratios for structural CDR and >300:1 for SRM peak‑shaving.

Overall, the document argues that planetary cooling is not optional but physically required to avoid irreversible cryosphere loss, AMOC collapse, and multi‑system tipping cascades. It reframes climate action from “stopping warming” to actively restoring Earth’s radiative balance and long‑term habitability.

title: Affective Equity and Evidentiary Legibility
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Affective Equity and Evidentiary Legibility
detail.abstract: AIVO's prior work (WP-2026-14, the Linkage Gap) established that AI systems cite a brand and then recommend a competitor 87.3 percent of the time across a corpus of more than 12,500 multi-turn purchase decision probes spanning 68 brands. That finding establishes that citation and recommendation are separable outcomes. It does not explain which brands are protected from displacement and which are not. This paper proposes that the explanation lies in a distinction between two forms of brand strength that are commonly treated as one. Affective Equity is the human-facing construct: sensory association, emotional memory, distinctive assets, and narrative resonance, the territory of classical brand equity theory. Evidentiary Legibility is the AI-facing construct: the density and structure of third-party-verifiable, attribute-level content available to an AI system evaluating a purchase decision. We hypothesize that Affective Equity predicts whether a brand is cited, consistent with recent third-party findings that longterm brand equity explains the majority of AI visibility, but that it does not predict whether a brand survives to become the final recommendation. We hypothesize that Evidentiary Legibility does predict survival, independent of Affective Equity, and that the Linkage Gap is concentrated among brands that are high on the former and low on the latter. We propose a method for testing this against AIVO's existing probe corpus and outline the construction of a new instrument, an Evidentiary Legibility score, required to run the analysis.

title: Medical Receivables as Counterparty Credit Risk: A Credibility-Theoretic Framework with a Calibration Gate

detail.title: Medical Receivables as Counterparty Credit Risk: A Credibility-Theoretic Framework with a Calibration Gate

No client or proprietary data is used in this paper; all quantitative content is closed-form theory or fully synthetic simulation.

detail.abstract: Medical receivables are conventionally managed as an operational-recovery problem: claims are worked by staff against denial-reason playbooks, and performance is measured as a recovery rate. This paper develops the theory of an alternative classification — a receivable is an exposure to an adjudicating counterparty — and derives what the classification makes decidable. Four sets of results. First, a two-level model of a claims book in which payer-level denial propensities carry the risk; the credibility estimator for a payer's propensity is derived from first principles, with shrinkage weight n_j/(n_j + m) and m = E[θ(1−θ)]/Var(θ), and the classical limited-fluctuation full-credibility standard is shown to reappear, exactly, as the refusal branch of the paper's speech-licensing gate. Second, the counterparty concentration hypothesis — claim-level features carry no outcome information conditional on payer identity — is formalized, and its testable signature proved: under the hypothesis the payer-only optimum attains the full-information optimum, so the population AUC gap is exactly zero; an exact pair decomposition shows what the finite-sample ablation can and cannot detect. Third, a calibration gate for validation: the volume inequality n ≥ p̂(1−p̂)(z/ε)², a turndown floor n_T = z²(1−p̂)/(γ²p̂) — the classical full-credibility standard redeployed as a refusal branch — below which the licensed output is refusal rather than a coarser number, an effective-volume rule n_eff = n/(1 + (ñ−1)ρ_ICC) pricing pooled fallback quotes under the model's own intraclass correlation, a push rule requiring the settlement map for multi-valued outcomes to be fixed ex ante (post-hoc settlement leaves the reported rate unidentified within an interval of width equal to the ambiguous mass), and judge–process independence. Fourth, the sharpest result: with payer-period shocks of variance share φ and persistence ρ, one-period-forward discrimination relates to within-period cross-validated discrimination by AUC_fwd ≈ Φ(κ Φ⁻¹(AUC_cv)) with κ = 1−(1−ρ)φ — so K-fold optimism on shock-driven books is structural, surviving correct specification and unlimited data; a companion result gives the Mills-ratio distortion of accepted-region calibration under selective labels. A fully synthetic, seeded simulation confirms each derived curve (the attenuation prediction is accurate to at most 0.021 AUC over a 3 × 5 parameter grid). Empirical validation on proprietary data is preregistered and reported separately.

title: Open Onchain University Vision
affiliations: Anadolu University

detail.title: Open Onchain University Vision
detail.abstract: Open and distance education has expanded access to higher learning for tens of millions of people, yet the evidence of that learning remains institutionally owned, administratively opaque, and difficult to verify across borders. This paper sets out the Open Onchain University (OOU), a design vision for an open, learner-owned credentialing and recognition infrastructure built on decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, and learning analytics. The paper is conceptual rather than empirical. It advances an earlier scoping review by the author on smart open education ecosystems (Fırat, 2023) from an account of technological potential to a specifiable infrastructure design, and revises several positions taken there. It develops a set of design principles, a five-layer reference architecture, a governance model, and a staged implementation roadmap, It formalizes the Proof-of-Learning construct as a five-tuple on which verification and recognition are defined as distinct operations, and it states each element of the design as a proposition that can be tested rather than as a claim that has been demonstrated. The central argument is deliberately narrow. Distributed ledger technology can make a claim about learning independently verifiable, but it cannot make that claim socially recognized, and the difference between verification and recognition is where earlier blockchain university proposals failed. OOU is therefore positioned not as a replacement for existing open universities but as a shared trust layer that established institutions, quality assurance bodies, and learner communities can adopt alongside emerging public infrastructures such as the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure. The paper gives equal weight to the constraints on this vision, including the tension between ledger immutability and the right to erasure identified by the European Data Protection Board, the credential-farming incentives created by tokenized rewards, the keymanagement burden placed on learners, and the risk that fine-grained credentialing accelerates the fragmentation of curricula that critics of micro-credentials have documented. Two configurations are proposed, one institutional and non-tokenized and one open and tokenized, so that the pedagogical architecture can be evaluated independently of the financial one.

title: Regional STEM Infrastructure and Financial Risks Facing Young People: A Panel Analysis of Kazakhstan's Regions
affiliations: , Nazarbayev Intellectual School of Physics and Mathematics in Aktobe, S Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, S Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University and Nazarbayev Intellectual School

detail.title: Regional STEM Infrastructure and Financial Risks Facing Young People: A Panel Analysis of Kazakhstan's Regions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The authors confirm that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This article examines the relationship between regional STEM infrastructure and the reconstructed volume of delinquent consumer debt among youth in the regions of the Republic of Kazakhstan from 2018 to 2024. The study is based on regional panel data, including indicators of STEM infrastructure, youth unemployment, household income, the share of the rural population, and characteristics of the regional consumer credit market. To assess statistical relationships, we use pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and a linear mixed model (LMM) with a random intercept at the regional level, which allows us to account for persistent interregional heterogeneity. The robustness of the results is tested using an alternative equally weighted STEM index, various scenarios for reconstructing the dependent variable, additional control for the scale of the regional consumer credit market, and a specification with a one-year lag of the STEM index. The pooled OLS results show a positive, statistically significant relationship between the STEM index and the reconstructed volume of delinquent debt among young people (β = 9.452, p = 0.022). However, after accounting for persistent regional heterogeneity in the LMM, the coefficient for the current STEM index decreases and becomes statistically insignificant (β = 4.795, p = 0.392). The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC = 0.620) indicates that regional clustering plays a significant role in the data structure. The main result holds when using an alternative equally-weighted STEM index and various scenarios for reconstructing the dependent variable. After additionally accounting for the size of the regional consumer credit market, the current STEM index also remains statistically insignificant (β = 0.830, p = 0.758), whereas the volume of consumer credit shows a positive, statistically significant relationship with reconstructed delinquent debt. The specification with a one-year lag of the STEM index yields a positive, statistically significant coefficient (β = 12.610; p = 0.043); however, this result is viewed as evidence of the sensitivity of the estimated relationship to the time specification and is not interpreted as a causal effect. The results show that the relationship between regional STEM infrastructure and youth credit risks, as observed at the aggregate level, depends significantly on accounting for persistent interregional differences, the size of the regional credit market, and the model's time specification. The study emphasizes the need to view STEM infrastructure as part of a broader regional educational, socioeconomic, and financial environment, rather than interpreting it as a direct determinant of young people's credit behavior.

title: Weather and Geopolitics Are Stress-Testing Europe's Clean Energy Transition: Wind, Water and the Price of the European Evening, 2015-2026

detail.title: Weather and Geopolitics Are Stress-Testing Europe's Clean Energy Transition: Wind, Water and the Price of the European Evening, 2015-2026
detail.abstract: European power prices are usually judged by an annual average. Read instead at the resolution the system runs at, one price per bidding zone per hour on a panel of 3.9 million zone-hours ending 10 August 2026, the clean transition has moved Europe's economic cycle in between a weather cycle and a political one. Summer 2026 had fifteen days on which ten or more of the 39 zones were hot at once against five in 2022, and heat reaches supply as well as demand. Fifteen of 35 river cooling sites ran at their lowest in 35 years, hydro's contribution to the evening climb halved from 8.9 to 4.3 GW, and gas covered the difference. Russian gas meanwhile fell from 42 per cent of extra-EU imports to about a tenth while liquefied gas rose to 44 per cent, a real diversification into a different form of exposure, and the defence budgets the same geopolitics requires draw on the fiscal space the grid needs. Solar carried the daytime this summer and cannot carry the evening, which falls to wind, hydro or fuel. Wind is the renewable whose share tracks national income, from 60 per cent of generation in Denmark to 1.4 in Hungary, so the member states with the widest gap between a cheap midday and a dear evening are the ones that have not built it. Adjacent zones clear at the same price in only 26 per cent of hours. Expanding wind, and building the wires and the agreement between zones that would let it be shared, is the binding constraint on completing the transition. This paper identifies that constraint from price and operating evidence, and it does not estimate the environmental or the total system cost of resolving it.

title: Chips and Megawatts: Structural Attribution in the AI Supply Chain, 2015-2026

detail.title: Chips and Megawatts: Structural Attribution in the AI Supply Chain, 2015-2026
detail.abstract: The artificial-intelligence supply chain is widely described as concentrated around its final buyers. This paper measures that description against a reference, comparing a 46-name basket of United States listings in every window of ten years against 200 control baskets drawn from the same sectors. Our analysis shows that the concentration is real and that it is not where the argument places it. Structural weight has been leaving the hyperscaler layer for a decade, by 6.4 percentage points, and accruing to the manufacturers of electrical equipment, whose order books track data-centre construction, while the regulated utilities usually bundled with them move the other way. The largest single gainer of the decade is a maker of grid apparatus rather than a chipmaker, and the migration replicates on European and Japanese universes against their own controls. The basket also behaves increasingly as one object rather than as 46 positions, which means less diversification inside a thematic sleeve than its name count suggests, although a category-driven explanation for that co-movement cannot be excluded by this design. Weight within the basket is distributed more unevenly than its co-movement accounts for, a result confined to United States listings. And while the basket falls roughly a quarter deeper than its sector peers when both fall, no network statistic anticipates when that happens, at any horizon between five and ninety days: these measures describe the present rather than forecast. Two methodological contributions travel beyond the case. Permutation against a matched control set is shown to be the appropriate inferential procedure for autocorrelated series of this kind, where interval estimates alone are insufficient. And networks inferred from raw market shares are shown to reproduce the signature of a captured ecosystem in the complete absence of any interaction, which bears on much of the visual argument currently made about this industry.

title: Globalization—Quo Vadis?
affiliations: Skidmore College - Department of Economics

detail.title: Globalization—Quo Vadis?
detail.abstract: The Global Financial Crisis of 2008–9 provided a critical watershed in the evolving global economic rebalancing and re-shifting towards China and Asia. The era of unchallenged US hegemony and “hyperglobalization” came to an end. Since 2017 the Sino-American geostrategic rivalry has taken centerstage in global affairs and is bound to play a decisive role in in the future evolution of globalization. Against the backdrop of Dani Rodrik’s (2011) “political trilemma of the world economy”, this essay reviews two recently published books on the subject matter of globalization that provide invaluable insights and strategic guidance into what is at stake. The first was published in November 2025, a single-authored work by Dani Rodrik titled “Shared Prosperity in a Fractured World: A New Economics for the Middle Class, the Global Poor, and Our Planet” (Princeton University Press). The second is a collection of contributions by expert economists co-edited by Lili Yan Ing and Dani Rodrik titled “The New Global Economic Order” (Routledge).
