detail.abstract: As the European Union diversifies its trade routes away from Russia, the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor is growing rapidly from a small base. This study asks how Bulgaria can convert its geographic position into measurable economic growth by activating the Poti-Varna-Ruse route, not as a low-cost rival to maritime shipping, which the evidence shows it cannot be, but as a predictable, EU-territory entry point with onward Danube distribution. Assessing the route against four criteria economic effect, predictability, legal-financial feasibility and geopolitical resilience and analysing the applicable EU instruments (TEN-T, CEF, GBER Article 56b, EGTC, Global Gateway), it benchmarks the plausible GDP effect against comparable transit economies and proposes a staged strategy governed by explicit decision thresholds. It treats the route's real constraints, Constanța's dominance, Georgian port limits, thin Bulgarian rail connectivity and conditional EU funding as binding design parameters. The contribution is an original, evidence-based synthesis showing that a capitalpoor state can turn its position on the map into durable growth by building from the constraints upward and drawing on instruments the Union already provides.

title: The Incomplete Gamma Continuation of the Reciprocal ξ-Function
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Incomplete Gamma Continuation of the Reciprocal ξ-Function
detail.abstract: Riemann's 1859 continuation writes ξ as a sum of incomplete gamma cells over the theta lattice, continued in the first argument of Γ(a, z). We derive the dual statement for the reciprocal 1/ξ(1 2 + √ s). Splitting the Lévy integral of its Thorin kernel at a free parameter τ , as Riemann split the Mellin integral at x = 1, gives a continuation whose cells are incomplete gamma functions of fixed first argument, continued in the second: exponential integrals Γ(0, •) over the ordinates, complementary error functions Γ(1 2 , •) over the log-prime lattice, and an entire Ein cell carrying the pole. Inversion swaps the two slots of the incomplete gamma, and the formula displays both lattices at once, where Riemann's keeps the zeros invisible. Two companion analyses accompany it. First, a classification: every displayed formula here is unconditional, and the Hypothesis enters only as the assertion that a lattice is real, a kernel completely monotone, or a transform a probability law. Second, a resolution of the factors of 1/ξ into Lévy and Thorin form by Pólya's 2 sin 2 lemma, with Bondesson's theorem, that a GGC transform is analytic and zero-free off the cut, as the instrument throughout. The archimedean factor is an extended GGC whose Thorin measure sits on the trivial zeros and whose symmetrization is unconditionally a Cauchy product; each local Euler factor is a compound Poisson law of stable(1 2) jumps with explicit but sign-changing Thorin density; and the cells of the continuation are infinitely divisible yet never Thorin, because cutting an integral destroys complete monotonicity of the kernel while preserving everything else. All identities are verified numerically to twelve digits.

title: NH-SOR: A Neuromorphic Heterogeneous Smart Order Router Compiled from Functional Realization Graphs
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: NH-SOR: A Neuromorphic Heterogeneous Smart Order Router Compiled from Functional Realization Graphs
detail.abstract: Framing. This is an architecture-and-modeling design study. No physical prototype exists; no system evaluated here-proposed or baseline-ran on physical hardware. All quantitative results are outputs of a single cycle-accurate event-driven simulation framework calibrated, parameterby-parameter, to published silicon and market-data measurements (provenance in Appendix C); they are projections, not achieved performance. Smart order routers (SORs) in fragmented equity markets face a latency-flexibility-compliance trilemma: software routers (10-50 µs tick-to-trade) are flexible but slow; FPGA routers (100-500 ns for minimal kernels) are fast but clock-bound and perception-blind; ASIC routers are fastest but immutable against evolving exchange protocols. We propose NH-SOR, a four-layer globally-asynchronous-locally-synchronous (GALS) architecture importing computational principles reverse-engineered from cortical circuits: (L1) a photonic ASIC sensory cortex transducing market photons into asynchronous address-events (8.5 ns); (L2) an FPGA thalamic gate performing cut-through decode, deterministic pre-trade risk control, and latency-coded spike encoding (17.5 ns, WCET-bounded); (L3) a neuromorphic cognitive core (262,144 LIF neurons; 64M Tsodyks-Markram synapses) implementing three FRG-compiled micro-circuits-a synaptic limit-order book, a bistable regime state-switch, and a winner-take-all venue selector ; (L4) an FPGA/ASIC motor cortex with photonic transmit. Micro-circuits are compiled from a formal Functional Realization Graph (FRG)-the requirements/capabilities bipartite graph of Yamakawa et al. (2024/2025)-for which we give, to our knowledge, the first complete formalization, validation metric arithmetic, and compilation algorithm. In calibrated simulation, NH-SOR projects mean tick-to-trade 86.0 ns (p99 112 ns), 4.7 W steady power, 310 Mev/s sustainable event rate, and 0.30-8.2 nJ per decision depending on the synaptic-energy technology scenario (0.38 nJ under our 7 nm projection; 3.3×-90× better per decision than the modeled FPGA baseline across scenarios). Regime shifts are detected at F1 = 0.86 within 94 ns versus 2.6-4.2 µs for CNN/LSTM baselines. We provide reconciled economic scenarios (break-even at $452B/yr routed notional against a $38M program), a scoped Reg NMS argument (architectural basis only; 15c3-5, CAT, and exchange certification out of scope; not legal advice), ablations with explicit interaction accounting, sensitivity sweeps, bootstrap CIs, and a costed roadmap. To our knowledge, based on the published literature, NH-SOR is the first architecture to embed validated brain-referenced spiking computation inside a regulation-bounded execution path.

title: Knowledge-base Modularity and Boundary Choice under Technological Discontinuity
affiliations: , SKEMA Business School and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) - Faculty of Business Administration (Munich School of Management)

detail.title: Knowledge-base Modularity and Boundary Choice under Technological Discontinuity
detail.abstract: How do firms choose between internal development and external sourcing when adopting AI-related technologies under technological discontinuity if a firm's knowledge base can be modular? We argue that knowledge-base modularity has two opposing effects on outsourcing: it initially increases outsourcing by reducing coordination and interface burdens, but at even higher levels it decreases outsourcing by raising the option value of internally retained, redeployable, and recombinable knowledge. We further argue that supplier capability distinctiveness under concentrated supply increases the level of modularity at which outsourcing is most attractive. Using patent data and outsourcing-event data on global automotive manufacturers in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving from 2000 to 2021, we find support for both predictions. We contribute by showing that modularity does not uniformly expand market use under technological discontinuity.

title: The Shifting Perimeter: Artificial Intelligence, Systemic Risk, and the Governance–Resilience Gap in Global Finance

detail.title: The Shifting Perimeter: Artificial Intelligence, Systemic Risk, and the Governance–Resilience Gap in Global Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research is conceptual and analytical in nature and does not involve human participants, patient data, or case studies requiring consent.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Financial regulators have spent the better part of a decade building an oversight vocabulary for artificial intelligence around fairness, explainability, and model risk. This chapter argues that this vocabulary, while necessary, was built to answer a different question than the one now confronting the financial system. The material risk emerging in 2025 and 2026 is not primarily that an AI model discriminates against a borrower or misclassifies a transaction; it is that a small number of AI infrastructure providers now sit underneath a large share of the world's financial operations, that AI-enabled cyberattacks move faster than existing incident-response protocols, and that correlated AI-driven trading or advisory behavior can amplify shocks across institutions that never directly interact. This is a resilience problem, not an ethics problem, and the two require different institutional answers. This chapter sets out the two regulatory logics, shows where they diverge, and previews how the book uses that divergence — rather than a single unified AI-governance narrative — as its organizing structure.

title: The Master of Ceremonies' Theorem
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Master of Ceremonies' Theorem
detail.abstract: In a chapter of Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!, a nightclub master of ceremonies teaches the physicist a three-part courtship protocol: transfer nothing before agreement, ask the decisive question at once, and display indifference. Feynman reports that it worked and that he abandoned it because using it made him feel bad. I analyze the anecdote as a bargaining problem in the tradition of Schelling (1960). The three rules prove to be separate results with different domains of validity: the first follows from a disagreementpoint comparative static, the second converts a war of attrition into an ultimatum and recovers the dissipated surplus, and the third violates single-crossing and is self-extinguishing. A Bayesian treatment shows that log posterior odds on a suitor's type accrue linearly in courtship duration and are invariant to fungible expenditure, so the drink has Bayes factor one. Linear drift makes the recipient's problem a sequential probability ratio test with optimal duration t * = [log(ℓ I /ℓ II)-log Ω 0 ]/(d + ι), from which follows a Tactician's Paradox: imitable manoeuvres reduce the information rate d, so tactical play lengthens courtship for everyone, including its practitioners. These tools dispose of the folk claim that courtship is a one-sided extraction of a man's time, money, and emotion. A calibration finds the traditional convention burning 99.94 of a prize worth 100, the larger share falling on the party the claim casts as beneficiary. Following Heaton and Polson (2012) on learning one's own type from price, I show the claim is self-sealing: separating it from the hypothesis that its holder is the type being screened out requires a self-directed prior he has set to zero, so no evidence revises it. Feynman's abandonment of a winning strategy is then rationalized as type selection in the sense of Frank (1988).

title: Temporal Logistic Classification of Dengue Risk: Post-Prediction Spatial Diagnostics and Intraurban Prioritization
affiliations: and University of São Paulo (USP) - Faculty of Economics, Administration and Accounting of Ribeirão Preto (FEARP)

detail.title: Temporal Logistic Classification of Dengue Risk: Post-Prediction Spatial Diagnostics and Intraurban Prioritization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by the Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior -- Brasil (CAPES), Finance Code 001.

detail.abstract: Epidemiological risk prediction has become increasingly important for strengthening public-health surveillance and supporting earlier, territorially informed responses. Although substantial research has advanced the understanding of factors associated with dengue propagation, dengue-related expenditures and productivity losses increased markedly over the last 12 years. This paper develops a temporally validated framework for dengue-risk classification, post-prediction spatial diagnostics, and intraurban operational prioritization. The framework integrates lagged epidemiological indicators, climatic conditions, seasonality, population, information access, digital connectivity, and territorial data within a binomial generalized linear model. Using monthly observations for all 5,570 Brazilian municipalities, the model was trained from 2001 to 2023 and evaluated out of sample from 2024 to 2025. It achieved an AUC of 0.888, PR-AUC of 0.778, balanced accuracy of 0.829, and F1-score of 0.723. Spatial diagnostics identified strong positive autocorrelation in mean predicted risk, while residual diagnostics indicated remaining territorial structure. A CNEFE-based layer subsequently translates municipal predictions into intraurban priority scores for surveillance coverage, active case search, and vector-control planning. The framework provides an interpretable and reproducible approach for geographically targeted dengue surveillance.

title: Bankrupting the Carceral State
affiliations: Harvard University, Harvard Law School

detail.title: Bankrupting the Carceral State

publicationDetails.detailsText: 23 Stanford Journal of Civil Rights & Civil Liberties _ (forthcoming 2027)

detail.abstract:
Chapter 11 ordinarily promises a forum for rehabilitating distressed debtors and distributing value among creditors. In private prison bankruptcies, however, it does something else: it shields agents of the carceral state from accountability.

Today, some of the nation’s largest private prison operators and carceral contractors are seeking refuge in Chapter 11. These corporations do not enter bankruptcy simply to rehabilitate failed enterprises. They enter to cabin liability. Upon filing, the bankruptcy case suspends litigation in non-bankruptcy fora—stalling prison lawsuits, halting discovery, and blocking the enforcement of judgments arising from systemic failures in prison management. For incarcerated plaintiffs seeking to vindicate their constitutional right to be free from “cruel and unusual punishments,” bankruptcy often marks the end of any meaningful path to justice.

Bankruptcy law is not typically understood as a domain of penal governance. Yet, as this Article shows, Chapter 11 has systemic carceral effects. Although Chapter 11 is unavailable to states and governmental units, carceral contractors—as agents of the carceral state exercising delegated coercive power—can invoke debtor protections reserved for private entities. Chapter 11 thus operates as the private-law infrastructure that keeps carceral markets intact, enabling contractors to continue extracting profit from captive populations while suppressing, under the guise of reorganization, the very claims that challenge that extraction. Once in bankruptcy, constitutional injuries are either extinguished or converted into unsecured claims. Those that survive bankruptcy’s initial procedural hurdles are processed through a regime that presumes mobility, resources, and legal sophistication that incarcerated people lack. Meanwhile, the business of confinement continues.

This Article is the first to examine how bankruptcy law intersects with the prison-industrial complex. It identifies four mechanisms through which carceral contractors deploy familiar tools of corporate reorganization to evade accountability: Freeze, Channel, Preserve, and Cleanse. “Freeze” captures the automatic stay’s power to stall or reshape litigation outside bankruptcy. “Channel” converts consti-tutional injuries into creditor claims through the claims-allowance process. “Preserve” maintains the debtor’s prepetition status quo by leaving management in control. “Cleanse” sheds liability through liability-management devices that cap recovery and protect non-debtor affiliates.

But bankruptcy is not only a tool of suppression. This Article argues that the same mechanisms can be turned against carceral corporate power. By leveraging bankruptcy courts’ equitable powers and targeted doctrinal reform, this Article develops a bankruptcy-centered abolitionist framework aimed at curbing carceral profiteering. In doing so, this Article reconceptualizes the carceral state as a supply chain: an enclosed market in which mass incarceration generates profit and bankruptcy law absorbs its costs.

title: Beyond Convenience: Smartphones and Household Saving-Borrowing Decisions
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: Beyond Convenience: Smartphones and Household Saving-Borrowing Decisions
detail.abstract: Using individual-level data from the 2024/2025 Global Findex Database across 140 economies, we show that smartphones shape household financial behavior through more than the ease and convenience of digital payments. We find that smartphone access significantly enhances financial vigilance and information-seeking behavior, and that this channel independently affects households' saving and borrowing decisions, even after accounting for digital payment usage and formal financial inclusion. Using economy fixed effects and a Lewbel (2012) heteroskedasticity-based instrumental variables strategy, our results are robust to reverse causality and omitted variable bias, with strong first-stage instruments throughout. A formal mediation test confirms that information-seeking and financial inclusion partially, but not fully, explain smartphones' direct effect on saving and borrowing. Collectively, our findings suggest that mobile technology's influence on household finance extends beyond transactional convenience: by fostering financial attentiveness, smartphones reshape core consumption-saving and borrowing decisions, indicating that mobile disruption plays a meaningful role in shaping key household financial choices.

title: F*** Everybody Who Isn't Us: Leveraging Ingroup Bias to Regulate AI**

detail.title: F*** Everybody Who Isn't Us: Leveraging Ingroup Bias to Regulate AI**

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None required
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
AI is booming because it is capitalist catnip. It increases corporate profits while employing fewer humans who can complain about their rights. It externalizes unmeasured risks onto the public and devours precious public resources. Unbridled neoliberalism is to blame, contributing to our burnout, loneliness, and extreme political polarization. This is exactly where the powers-that-be want us. We are so disconnected and divided that we direct our hostility toward each other rather than toward the tech billionaires whose philosophy is to “f*** everybody who isn’t us.” It is time we flip the script. 

 

This Article proposes harnessing humans’ innate ingroup bias, not against one another, but against AI. By recasting AI systems and the corporations that develop them as a disembodied and unfeeling outgroup, warring political factions can unite around one achievable goal—subordinating AI before its rights surpass our own. We must discriminate against AI to regulate it heavily and prioritize human flourishing. If there ever were an issue to unite a painfully polarized country, that issue is reclaiming our human voices against the threats of AI.

 

Drawing on the psychology of collective action and ingroup bias, this Article explains how such a coalition could form and what its political messaging must contain. To justify the discrimination I propose, I call for an immediate moratorium on developing sentient and feeling AI. The choice is stark. We must organize now or sleepwalk into a dystopian future where our jobs are displaced by AI and we are experimented upon, without our consent. The devil is not, as they say, in the details. The devil is in the macro-economic policy that needs to be completely turned on its head.

title: "The European Union's Dublin Regulation" in The Sage Encyclopedia of Refugee Studies (2025).
affiliations: St. John's University - School of Law

detail.title: "The European Union's Dublin Regulation" in The Sage Encyclopedia of Refugee Studies (2025).
detail.abstract: The European Union’s Dublin Regulation determines which member state is responsible for examining an asylum seeker’s claims for protection in the EU. The Regulation is an essential feature of the Common European Asylum System (CEAS), which aims to promote an equitable, harmonized approach for dealing with protection claims lodged by third-country nationals and stateless persons. This entry describes the Regulation’s historical context, responsibility allocation criteria, and common criticisms.

title: Downside and Volatility Risk Premia in Derivatives Markets: Quantitative Strategies and Hedge-Fund Trading Behaviour

detail.title: Downside and Volatility Risk Premia in Derivatives Markets: Quantitative Strategies and Hedge-Fund Trading Behaviour
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified empirical framework for studying how ownership structure and managerial incentives shape asset prices, and for testing whether the resulting risk premia are priced and traded in derivatives markets. The design spans three economies at different stages of financial development: India, the United States, and Australia. The theoretical anchor is the dynamic contracting equilibrium of Jung, Subramanian and Zeng (2024), in which a large blockholder trades discretely, small shareholders trade continuously, and long-term incentive contracts tie managerial compensation to firm value. The model implies that performance-pay sensitivity (PPS) and block ownership are negatively associated with expected returns, return volatility, and Sharpe ratios, and positively associated with each other. These cross-sectional predictions have not been tested, because the model stops short of a multi-firm equilibrium. We translate the predictions into three studies. Study 1 tests the ownership-PPS-return relations in the cross-section of NSE/BSE, S&P; 500, and S&P;/ASX 200 firms using a Fama-MacBeth design augmented with single-and multi-factor benchmarks. Study 2 asks whether option-implied moments and variance risk premia differ systematically with ownership concentration, using model-free implied moments (Bakshi, Kapadia and Madan, 2003), variance swaps (Carr and Wu, 2009), and implied-realised volatility spreads (Bali and Hovakimian, 2009). Study 3 examines whether quantitative strategies that harvest volatility and downside premia, including delta-hedged option writing, variance selling, and downside-protected factor portfolios, are profitable after hedging costs, and whether observed trading behaviour-option-writing patterns of hedge funds in the Agarwal-Naik tradition, and the unusually large retail short-option flows in India-are consistent with those returns. The paper contributes the first three-market test of the Jung-Subramanian-Zeng predictions across an ownership spectrum running from near-half-of-equity promoter holdings in India to the diffuse US cross-section; connects ownership structure to derivatives prices; quantifies the strategies that harvest the premia with explicit accounting for hedging costs under classical and machine-learning pricing models; and uses the Indian setting, where the world's largest retail derivatives market provides a unique laboratory for studying who earns the variance risk premium.

title: Stagflation Reconsidered: Demand Constraint, the Asset System, and Cost Transmission

detail.title: Stagflation Reconsidered: Demand Constraint, the Asset System, and Cost Transmission
detail.abstract: Stagflation-the simultaneous occurrence of stagnant growth and rising prices-has resisted satisfactory explanation for half a century. Supply-shock accounts identify the trigger but not the structural precondition that determines why the same shock produces very different outcomes across economies and time periods. Monetarist accounts explain why inflation can become entrenched but not why it coincides with demand contraction rather than demand expansion. Sellers' inflation accounts accurately describe the microeconomic transmission mechanism but leave unexplained why the economy was in a state where that mechanism could operate with such force. This paper argues that stagflation is not an anomalous combination of two independent disturbances but a predictable boundary state of the demand-constrained economy: the point at which cost pressures accumulated in the asset system during an extended period of monetary expansion finally transmit into the production system, while the underlying demand deficiency remains unrepaired. The transmission proceeds through five stages: demand constraint generating reliance on monetary expansion and external demand substitutes; new money flowing into the asset system rather than the production system; asset-system inflation progressively restructuring the cost base of the production system through four channels-land and real estate costs, capital return expectations, the urban labor cost premium, and the fiscal structure; an external trigger detonating the accumulated cost pressures; and the resulting cost-push inflation coinciding with, and deepening, demand weakness through the wage-price spiral. This account resolves several puzzles that alternative explanations cannot: why stagflation is specific to demand-constrained economies with extended prior monetary expansion; why it emerges with a significant lag after monetary expansion begins; why the same supply shock produces stagflation in economies where Stage Three has advanced and only temporary inflation in those where it has not; why it is so difficult to cure without worsening the contraction; and why the resolution of both the 1970s episode and the 2021-23 episode did not eliminate demand constraint but merely relocated it. The framework is applied to the US experience of the 1970s and the 2021-23 inflation episode, and is situated in relation to supply-shock theory, monetarism, sellers' inflation, and Modern Monetary Theory. The paper concludes that the structural precondition for stagflation recurrence-demand constraint sustained by asset-system expansion that progressively restructures the cost base-has not been resolved in most advanced economies, and that addressing it requires structural repair of the mechanisms through which production generates adequate income to sustain demand endogenously.

title: When Profit is Not Distributable: Externality Residuals, Distributive Incompleteness, and Payout Governance

detail.title: When Profit is Not Distributable: Externality Residuals, Distributive Incompleteness, and Payout Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual study and does not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental procedures requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Financial reporting separates measured earnings from resources available for payout. Sustainability reporting can expose attributable external costs without classifying their distributional status. This paper asks when that gap becomes a distinct accounting problem and how it can be governed without expanding liability recognition or redefining earnings. Using problem-driven conceptual analysis, it defines distributive incompleteness only relative to an adopted payout-protection objective: an eligible residual survives recognition and settlement, the objective requires resource backing, and no traceable payout classification implements that requirement. Externality Reserve Accounting (ERA) represents this narrow domain through an item-level residual register, contractibility conditions of observability, verifiability, and enforceability, an institutionally authorized coverage rule, and a reserve roll-forward. The analysis establishes that residual measurement is distinct from coverage authority and derives a recognition-handoff result: when the same residual later becomes an equity-reducing recognized obligation, releasing the covered ERA amount prevents double counting; under full coverage, payout capacity is invariant at the handoff. ERA is therefore a bounded, falsifiable theory of intertemporal payout classification rather than a universal sustainability reserve.

title: Railway Lines and Commuter Flows: Evidence from Line Reactivations in Germany

detail.title: Railway Lines and Commuter Flows: Evidence from Line Reactivations in Germany
detail.abstract: What is the impact of railway lines on commuter flows? This paper analyses the effects of reactivating railway lines on inter-municipal commuting patterns in Germany between 2002 and 2024. The empirical strategy combines a linear difference-in-differences approach for aggregate outcomes at the municipality level with a non-linear gravity model for bilateral flows at the municipality pair level, comparing directly connected municipalities to those located along lines recommended for reactivation but not yet implemented. The results indicate no significant change in aggregate commuter volumes and general bilateral flows, regardless of service frequency. Statistically significant increases in commuting intensity are observed primarily for initially strong commuter flows. This suggests that railway line reactivations intensify pre-existing commuter paths rather than establish new economic links.

title: A Decision-theoretic Framework for Adaptive Tutoring: Grounded Content Generation, Risk-controlled Delivery, and Formal Guarantees

detail.title: A Decision-theoretic Framework for Adaptive Tutoring: Grounded Content Generation, Risk-controlled Delivery, and Formal Guarantees

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human subjects and uses no participant data; all quantitative results derive from a fully disclosed synthetic simulation. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: We study adaptive tutoring—deciding, turn by turn and under uncertainty, how to sequence and pace instruction for an individual learner—as a formal decision problem, and give a decision-theoretic framework with stated guarantees. The framework has two coupled parts. A lesson compiler turns a minimal input (a sentence, a paragraph, an image, a topic, or a content pack) into an Adaptive Lesson Graph under a sentence-level grounding gate that admits only content entailed by the author's source. A delivery controller then treats tutoring as a partially observable decision process over a latent learner state—per-concept mastery and an engagement variable—inferred from response correctness and, as a bounded-reliability measurement, facial-action and vocal-prosody features. The controller advances through a conformally calibrated mastery gate (with a bounded-repeat liveness escape), selects diagnostics by an information-gain criterion, and is constrained to break detected disengagement within one step, giving a progress-or-intervene termination guarantee. We state the properties the design provides—grounding faithfulness under an entailment assumption; distribution-free coverage of gate-triggered advancement under exchangeability; optimality of greedy diagnostic selection (exact under the factored belief, (1-1/e) in the correlated case); bounded-repeat termination; and deterministic replayability for audit—each with the assumptions it requires. Because we deliberately do not treat emotion read from faces as ground truth, affect enters only as a bounded-reliability signal, and we quantify how the controller behaves as that reliability degrades. A fully disclosed synthetic simulation (a generative learner model, not human-subjects data) illustrates the mechanism: sensitivity to the engagement signal lowers the fraction of interactions spent disengaged by about 61% at equal-or-higher mastery and equal interaction cost, and the benefit is essentially flat across measurement noise. We are explicit throughout about which claims are proved, which are simulated, and which await a human-subjects test, and about the scientific and ethical limits of inferring affect from behavior.

title: When Scale Outruns Fees: The Scale–Fee-Density Paradox in China’s Trust Industry

detail.title: When Scale Outruns Fees: The Scale–Fee-Density Paradox in China’s Trust Industry
detail.abstract: China's trust industry has returned to asset growth while its fee-generating capacity has not expanded at the same pace. This study documents that divergence using a balanced panel of nine trust institutions with scope-consistent public disclosures from 2021 to 2025 (45 firm-years). On a contemporaneous year-end basis, these institutions held RMB4.87 trillion of trust assets in 2021 (23.7% of the industry total) and RMB8.08 trillion in 2024 (27.3%). The primary measure is fee density: annual trust-business or net fee income divided by year-end trust assets under management (AUM), expressed in basis points. Across institutions, median cumulative AUM growth was 117.1%, whereas median fee-income growth was-32.8% and median fee density fell by 62.2%. Fee density declined at all nine institutions, yielding an exact two-sided sign-test pvalue of 0.0039. A two-way fixed-effects log specification estimates an elasticity of fee income with respect to AUM of 0.623 (homoskedastic standard error 0.185), below the proportional benchmark of one. Point estimates remain below one across alternative windows, first differences, exclusion of explicitly caveated observations, and leave-one-institution-out checks, although the estimate excluding one influential institution is not distinguishable from proportional scaling. The evidence therefore supports a consistent descriptive pattern of scale-fee dilution, with magnitudes that vary across sample perturbations. It does not identify a causal mechanism and does not equate fee density with accounting profitability. The findings suggest that AUM growth is an incomplete performance signal during a transition toward asset-service and standardized asset-management activities.

title: Time Poverty, Waiting, and Broadband Adoption: Evidence From the US by Gender and Income
affiliations: , Independent and Rutgers University, New Brunswick

detail.title: Time Poverty, Waiting, and Broadband Adoption: Evidence From the US by Gender and Income

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this analysis of publicly available data.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by funding from the New Jersey Policy Lab.

detail.abstract: Despite longer lifespans, many people keep feeling “time poor,” often struggling to complete daily tasks. This challenge is most pronounced among women, who frequently have disproportionate domestic labor responsibilities, and low-income individuals, who frequently lack the resources to outsource time-intensive activities. As time poverty reinforces and perpetuates social inequalities, policies to alleviate it, such as reducing time spent on errands like queuing for goods and services, can play a key role in addressing these disparities. In this context, we explore the potential of expanding broadband adoption as a possible policy solution as it may enable more efficient access to goods and services online, thereby reducing waiting times. Integrating broadband data with diary records from the American Time Use Survey, we construct a 14-year panel dataset (2008–2021) and estimate a fixed effect model. We further examine the impact for broadband by gender and income. Findings contribute to policies intending to alleviate time poverty by demonstrating that living in connected counties reduces time spent waiting for goods and services, with the effect being particularly pronounced among women. However, we also highlight the need for complementary policy measures to fully address persistent disparities. Our results are robust to different model specifications and an instrumental variable approach.

title: Five Stages of the Public Discourse on Artificial Intelligence: An Analytical Grid for 2026

detail.title: Five Stages of the Public Discourse on Artificial Intelligence: An Analytical Grid for 2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal conflict of interest relevant to this work.

detail.abstract: Public debate on artificial intelligence in Francophone Europe suffers from a categorical confusion that renders the most rigorous analyses inaudible and amplifies the most obsolete positions. Media commentary without effective practice receives the same presumed authority as theorisation from cumulative intensive use, though the two positions share neither the same epistemic value nor the same relation to the object they claim to describe. This note proposes, as an essay, a five-stage grid restoring that distinction without polemic. The stages are T00 (structural blocking from access), T0 (commentary drawn from an obsolete state of the art), T1 (journalistic–analytic reporting), T2 (transversal theorisation of what AI reconfigures across domains) and T3 (theorisation articulated to intensive practice). The grid is monotonic in position, not in wisdom; a given author may occupy different positions across corpora or move between stages over time. Empirical implications discussed include the composition of French parliamentary AI commissions, the position from which European regulatory decisions are taken, and the projected trajectory of a generation trained under "zero AI" organisational policies during critical developmental years, read against the analogy of 1980s Soviet informatics.

title: Reassessing the Fed Put State-Dependent Monetary Transmission around FOMC Announcements

detail.title: Reassessing the Fed Put State-Dependent Monetary Transmission around FOMC Announcements
detail.abstract: We reassess the Fed Put using intraday futures data around 116 FOMC announcements from 2010 to 2024. We adapt the Conditional Average Response (CAR) estimator of Gonçalves et al. (2024) to high-frequency event studies and develop event-level bootstrap inference for a cross-asset nonlinear functional of nonparametric responses. This is the first application of the CAR framework outside the fiscal-multiplier setting. Our main empirical finding is a state-dependent attenuation of Treasury transmission. Under the pure monetary policy shocks of Jarociński and Karadi (2020), the ten-year note response is about 21 basis points smaller in stressed markets, survives episode-clustered inference, and is the only member of our pre-specified family to survive familywise correction. We also decompose the equity response into a Treasury-implied rate component and a benchmark-relative residual. The residual reaches 31 basis points in stressed markets, declines as benchmark duration shortens, and is not separately identified against a money-market strip. Calibrated simulations show conservative inference and low power at the empirical sample size. The results show that state-dependent monetary transmission depends on both the economic estimand and the benchmark used to define it.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Mainstream Technical Indicators for Whipsaw Detection in Tactical Equity Strategies

detail.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Mainstream Technical Indicators for Whipsaw Detection in Tactical Equity Strategies
detail.abstract:
All tactical equity systems that rotate assets based on risk management share a common vulnerability: in range-bound, directionless markets — commonly termed whipsaws — the same rotation logic that generates profit in trending environments instead produces a sequence of costly, unprofitable reversals. Practitioners have long relied on a family of price-derived technical indicators to detect these conditions, including the Choppiness Index, the Average Directional Index (ADX), the Kaufman Efficiency Ratio, the Hurst Exponent, and Bollinger Band Width, typically deployed at their commonly cited default parameterizations. This paper subjects that toolkit to a rigorous, economically grounded test: using 26 years of daily SPY price data (2000–2026) and a real, dollar-denominated trading record spanning 18 years, we evaluate each indicator's ability to discriminate between genuine whipsaw conditions and trending markets, its sensitivity to lookback-window selection, its resistance to overfitting under honest cross-validation, and its ultimate economic value when assembled into a composite detection system and back-tested against 36 real, dollar-measured episodes of whipsaw-driven trading losses.

The central findings are threefold. First, at their commonly cited default parameters, none of the indicators tested achieve statistically meaningful separation between whipsaw and trending conditions — several are statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip. Second, properly tuned via honest cross-validation, performance improves substantially, but only by adopting lookback windows (80–100 trading days) considerably longer than practitioner convention, and even then, several indicators exhibit a textbook overfitting signature: performance that improves monotonically on training data while degrading on genuinely held-out data. Third, when assembled into a composite detection system and evaluated on real economic outcomes, the resulting detector achieves a positive net benefit but requires substantially more total trading days in a defensive posture to achieve it, with a correspondingly higher rate of false alarms during genuine trending markets, than the underlying economics would ideally tolerate. We conclude that the mainstream price-based toolkit, while not without value, has real and measurable limitations for this specific application, and we close with a brief note on a promising alternative signal family — currently under separate development — that appears to address several of these limitations directly.

title: The Value of Influence Data
affiliations: Jinan University, Huazhong University of Science and Technology - School of Economics and Independent

detail.title: The Value of Influence Data
detail.abstract: This paper studies how a monopolist acquires consumer-level influence data to personalize prices in a market with positive network externalities. For any acquired dataset, the firm's profit depends on an effective data variance measuring the resolved influence heterogeneity. The optimal untargeted set therefore forms an interval: the monopolist leaves intermediate types unidentified while targeting one or both tails of the influence distribution. The value of influence data is higher in denser or more dispersed networks, and the targeted set expands as data become cheaper or network effects become stronger. The acquisition technology is consequential. Compared with representative random sampling which induces an all-or-nothing acquisition strategy, targeting supports partial acquisition and raises both profit and aggregate consumer surplus when data are costly; When data are cheap, targeting benefits the firm but reduces consumer surplus, yielding an ambiguous welfare impact.

title: Are Housing Values Higher in U.S Counties with Vibrant Arts and Culture?
affiliations: University of Maine - School of Economics, University of Maine and University of Maine - School of Economics

detail.title: Are Housing Values Higher in U.S Counties with Vibrant Arts and Culture?

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between housing values and the arts and cultural vitality of U.S. counties. Arts and culture are represented by novel measures based upon the number of projects funded by the National Endowment for the Arts and the National Endowment for the Humanities and the number of entries on the National Register of Historic Places. These three measures of arts and culture cover about 233,000 projects and places, which is a substantially higher number compared to the 18,800 U.S. establishments in the performing arts (NAICS 7111) and museums (NAICS 712) sectors. Empirical results show a positive, statistically significant, and economically meaningful relationship between median housing values and a composite index of arts and culturee.g., a one-standard deviation increase in this variable is associated with 3.4 percent higher housing values. Extensions to the main analysis show larger impacts on housing values associated with arts (compared to measures of culture and cultural heritage), and larger impacts in metropolitan counties versus non-metro areas.

title: Power and Behavior in Infrastructure Projects: Explaining the Emergence, Continuation, and Transition of Behavioral-Institutional Response Logics
affiliations: Curtin University - School of Civil and Mechanical Engineering

detail.title: Power and Behavior in Infrastructure Projects: Explaining the Emergence, Continuation, and Transition of Behavioral-Institutional Response Logics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: Note applicable
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Cost misperformance remains a recurrent feature of infrastructure procurement for publicsector agencies, yet limited attention has been paid to how power shapes organizational responses to recognized cost pressures. Drawing on the Fifth Hand, we examine how four behavioral-institutional response logics-Benevolent, Protective, Passive, and Malevolentemerge, continue, and transition during project development and delivery. We conduct a process-oriented comparative case study of two Australian hospital projects with contrasting procurement and governance arrangements, drawing on Auditor-General reports. Temporal reconstruction shows that recognition of cost pressure alone does not alter the prevailing response logic. Power becomes consequential through configurations of authority, expertise, information, dependency, and contractual rights that enable actors to sustain, challenge, or redirect the prevailing response. A response continues as long as these configurations reproduce the conditions that support it, while a transition becomes possible as changes alter actors' capacity or willingness to act. Our study provides a temporal process explanation for the Fifth Hand, demonstrating how power and contractual governance shape response trajectories and infrastructure project cost outcomes.

title: Structural Inertia and Market Friction in Global Fossil Fuel Trade: A Longitudinal Network Analysis of Resource Path Dependencies
affiliations: Telkom University, Telkom University and Telkom University

detail.title: Structural Inertia and Market Friction in Global Fossil Fuel Trade: A Longitudinal Network Analysis of Resource Path Dependencies
detail.abstract: Achieving global decarbonization targets requires a fundamental structural transformation of global resource supply chains. Despite growing commitments under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), fossil fuels continue to dominate international commerce through deeply embedded trade architectures. This study examines the structural elasticity of global coal, crude oil, and natural gas networks in response to sustainability-driven mandates. Using longitudinal network analysis of 216 monthly bilateral trade observations (2007-2024), we employ density, modularity, and centrality metrics as structural economic diagnostics, and validate the central claim with a four-step identification strategy combining Bai-Perron multiple structural break detection, interrupted time-series regressions controlled for Brent prices, geopolitical risk, and global growth, placebo intervention dates, and a first-differenced specification. The results demonstrate that these networks remain structurally persistent despite policy intent: crude oil maintains a cohesive global topology, natural gas exhibits increasing regional consolidation, and coal shows uneven contraction. We find that structural reconfiguration occurs primarily in response to exogenous market shocks-such as the 2008 financial crisis and the Russia-Ukraine conflict-rather than to policy implementation. A formal identification battery confirms this: once macroeconomic controls and placebo intervention dates are applied, SDG adoption produces no detectable structural break, and any apparent post-2015 effect does not survive first-differencing. We identify network-mediated carbon lock-in as a critical market friction that limits the effectiveness of decarbonization strategies. Integrating these network diagnostics into resource policy evaluation provides a necessary framework for stress-testing transition pathways and designing coordinated trade and climate instruments.

title: Secure E-Waste Collection Networks in Egypt: A Stochastic Analysis of Recovery-Leakage Trade-offs

detail.title: Secure E-Waste Collection Networks in Egypt: A Stochastic Analysis of Recovery-Leakage Trade-offs
detail.abstract: This computational study evaluates how collection density, traceability, security controls, workforce skills, recovery capacity, and regulatory support interact in a secure electronic-waste collection network. A transparent synthetic dataset of 450 network cases was generated to validate the analytical architecture before field deployment. The readiness model explained 45.7% of variance; the recovery and leakage models explained 69.2% and 74.4%, respectively. Collection density produced the largest readiness coefficient, while security controls and traceability were central to limiting diversion. Mean recovery increased from 54.1% in the low-security tier to 62.1% in the high-security tier, and leakage declined from 36.3% to 22.3%. The findings show that collection coverage alone is insufficient: custody controls, event traceability, workforce competence, and treatment capacity must be designed as complementary capabilities. The values are synthetic and should be interpreted as computational method-validation evidence rather than estimates of Egypt’s actual e-waste system.

title: The Null Player's Tailwind: Passive Return, Efficient Prices, and Just Deserts

detail.title: The Null Player's Tailwind: Passive Return, Efficient Prices, and Just Deserts
detail.abstract: How can a beneficiary with no intelligence, information, portfolio choice, or managerial activity receive the long-run return on a broad stock-market index? This note separates the productive asset from its passive claimant and then combines a contribution test with elementary market arithmetic. A capitalization-weighted total-market portfolio is the market's dollar-weighted average, so its gross return relative to that same market benchmark is zero by identity. Semi-strong efficient-market reasoning removes public information as a source of personal informational contribution. A corrected null-claimant theorem shows that beneficiary identity is not an input into the production of the portfolio's cash flows, while a construction of compelled heirs establishes the narrower nullity of the discretionary act of choosing a benchmark that a mechanical rule would have implemented anyway, and of the abstinence that would otherwise be offered in its place. Finally, an exact long-horizon decomposition shows that, unless valuation multiples grow or shrink exponentially without bound, persistent total-market compounding must be sustained by distributions and growth in the underlying per-unit fundamental base. The positive benchmark return received by a passive beneficiary in the funded benchmark arrangement considered here is therefore a participation return on the aggregate productive economy, the American Tailwind, and not evidence of exceptional personal informational, selection, managerial, or entrepreneurial contribution. The result establishes a boundary for contribution-based theories of just deserts. It does not deny that productive capital earns a return, that risk affects prices, that portfolio choice can be valuable, or that legal ownership has consequences. Practical alpha is retained as a deliberately generous safe harbor for possible personal creation. The further conclusion that the republic should receive the inherited benchmark remainder requires an additional normative property principle, supplied in companion papers and stated explicitly where it is used here.

title: No ESG, No Problem? Evidence from the Stock Market's Reaction to Financial Penalties
affiliations: Quinnipiac University School of Business and Charles University in Prague, Faculty of Social Sciences, Institute of Economic Studies, Students

detail.title: No ESG, No Problem? Evidence from the Stock Market's Reaction to Financial Penalties
detail.abstract: This study investigates the stock market's reaction to official announcements of penalties for corporate misconduct related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG). Using a large dataset spanning multiple decades, we initially find no reaction to penalty announcements, consistent with prior literature. However, we show that this result is driven by the aggregation of penalty types: we find a significantly negative market response to environmental penalties but no response to social and governance penalties. When we disaggregate further, we find a significant negative reaction to specific sub-types of social and governance penalties that is masked by aggregation. Next, using quantile regressions, we examine the relation between stock returns and penalty characteristics across the distribution of abnormal returns. This analysis reveals that the market reacts negatively to some penalty announcements and positively to others, shedding light on the lack of market reaction documented in prior studies. We identify several firm-and penaltyspecific characteristics, such as penalty size and recidivism, that explain variation in abnormal returns around official penalty announcements and find that their impact varies across the distribution of abnormal returns and across days in the event window. Overall, our results highlight the importance of accounting for heterogeneity in penalty samples and provide novel insights into market reactions to corporate misconduct.

title: The Granularity of Price Discovery: Firm-Specific and Local-Market Information in Public and Private Valuations
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Granularity of Price Discovery: Firm-Specific and Local-Market Information in Public and Private Valuations
detail.abstract: We ask at what level public equity prices anticipate future operating fundamentals: the markets in which firms invest or the firms themselves. Using apartment REITs, we combine public valuations, private transaction capitalization rates, and subsequent net operating income. Public valuations predict future income growth. In a smaller matched sample, private valuations do not forecast income in the direction implied by cash-flow anticipation. At two years, essentially all public predictive content is firm-specific, with none detectable in the local-market component. Price discovery about fundamentals is granular.

title: Probabilistic Assessment of Interconnection Cost Exposure for ERCOT Data Centers under Senate Bill 6
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Probabilistic Assessment of Interconnection Cost Exposure for ERCOT Data Centers under Senate Bill 6

declarations.funderStatement: Not funded

detail.abstract:
Texas’s large-load interconnection queue grew nearly fourfold in a single year, from roughly 63 GW at the end of 2024 to over 233 GW by December 2025, more than 70% of it data centers. This growth prompted the Texas Legislature’s Senate Bill 6 (SB 6) and the Public Utility Commission of Texas’s (PUCT) implementing rulemaking (Project No. 58481). Both address two of the three interconnection cost components a developer owes: a $50,000/MW interconnection fee and a tiered study fee. The third, Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC), covers 100% of direct network-upgrade costs and has no published formula. This gap is consistent with a broader literature finding that network-upgrade cost allocation, rather than fixed fees, drives interconnection-project risk and attrition. This study develops a Monte Carlo model of total interconnection cost exposure for a representative 75–200 MW ERCOT data-center project, structuring CIAC uncertainty by nodal congestion tier. Across 200,000 simulated projects, median exposure is $19.1M (P10–P90: $9.2M–$58.9M), or 1.4% of facility capital, rising to a median of $48.9M (3.6%) on the most congested nodes. The tier medians independently bracket published generator-interconnection cost benchmarks ($40–$350/kW modeled, versus $73/kW completed and $373/kW withdrawn nationally), an out-of-sample cross-check the model was not designed to satisfy.
The result is a quantitative demonstration that SB 6’s cost-allocation framework is procedurally complete but not planning-complete, and a reproducible tool for tracking that gap as PUCT finalizes the rule, expected later in 2026, and as the first Batch 1 interconnection agreements under it begin executing in 2027.

title: Document, Document, Document: Authorship Provenance as an Eligibility Criterion in Public Education

detail.title: Document, Document, Document: Authorship Provenance as an Eligibility Criterion in Public Education
detail.abstract: The literature on artificial intelligence detection is a literature about detectors, asking whether classifiers are accurate and whose writing they misread. Underneath that contest sits a remedy on which nearly everyone agrees. Keep your version history. Compose inside a tool that logs your process. Be able to show your work. Integrity offices, vendors, journalists, and the writers who attack detection most sharply all give the same advice, and all of them offer it as neutral prudence. This Article is about the advice. Process-logging instruments authenticate authorship by inspecting how text entered a document. Grammarly Authorship sorts every character into a fixed taxonomy: typed by a human, generated by artificial intelligence, modified or edited with it, or pasted from a known or unknown source. There is no category for text that was spoken. Google Workspace for Education, the dominant platform in American K-12 schooling, ships no authorship tool at all; its Originality Reports check for copied text rather than machine authorship, and the record teachers actually consult is Google Docs version history, which logs a large insertion with a timestamp and supplies no label for it. Dictated text arrives as a block. It is scored as an unattributed paste, or left unlabeled for a human to interpret privately. The research program underwriting these instruments states the defect in its own vocabulary, because educational measurement researchers have built keystroke classifiers separating original composition from reproduction, and the published feature sets enumerate insertions, deletions, pauses, and pastes with dictation nowhere in the list. An accommodation is a different process. That is what an accommodation is, and in a school the difference is legally required, individually determined, and written down by the entity that will later evaluate the work. This Article makes three claims. First, that process-based provenance measures input mechanism and reports the result as authorship, and that published demonstrations of trivial evasion establish the gap rather than suggesting it. Second, that a documentation requirement applied as a condition of academic evaluation is an eligibility criterion under 28 C.F.R. §35.130(b)(8) and must be shown necessary, which is already settled law where documentation burdens fall on disabled students. Third, that the school case is the strongest configuration of this problem anywhere in the detection literature, because the defendant is a public entity, the individualized education program closes the knowledge element, Perez v. Sturgis Public Schools clears exhaustion, and Payan preserves the one category of damages surviving Cummings.

title: American Social Capitalism: A Policy Framework for Competitive Markets, Universal Social Insurance, and Fiscal Responsibility

detail.title: American Social Capitalism: A Policy Framework for Competitive Markets, Universal Social Insurance, and Fiscal Responsibility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial conflicts of interest or personal relationships that could have influenced the content of this work. This paper represents an independently developed policy analysis and framework.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work does not involve human subjects, animal research, clinical data, or experiments requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was independently developed by the author.

detail.abstract:
American Social Capitalism presents an independently developed policy framework designed to preserve competitive markets while strengthening social insurance and long-term fiscal responsibility. The framework examines how the United States can combine private ownership, entrepreneurship, and market competition with broad-based protections against major economic risks, including healthcare costs, disability, unemployment, poverty in old age, and childhood hardship.

The paper evaluates policy options across three fiscal scenarios—cautious, baseline, and optimistic—using estimates from government and independent policy sources. It identifies areas where official scores exist and clearly distinguishes modeled assumptions where no formal score is available.

This white paper is not a peer-reviewed academic study. It is intended to contribute to public policy discussion regarding economic competitiveness, social insurance, healthcare reform, and fiscal sustainability.

title: Alignment Gaps Between Passive ESG Index Allocation and Science-Based Climate Targets: An Empirical Assessment of iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF and SBTi Commitments

detail.title: Alignment Gaps Between Passive ESG Index Allocation and Science-Based Climate Targets: An Empirical Assessment of iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF and SBTi Commitments
detail.abstract: This study investigates the structural alignment between index-based Environ mental, Social, and Governance (ESG) portfolio allocations and science-based decarbonization commitments. Utilizing an automated multi-anchor entity resolution pipeline (ISIN, LEI, Name), we link the portfolio holdings of the iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF (ESGU) across a 12-quarter window (Q1 2023–Q4 2025) with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) database, yielding a total of 552 entity-status observation units (Nobs). The entity resolution framework achieves high precision, yielding 36.23% confirmed matches ( A1, primarily driven by deterministic ISIN linkage) and 3.80% provisional matches (A2), while 59.96% (A3) remain unmatched (not registered). Sen sitivity analysis demonstrates that a string similarity threshold of τ = 0.96 serves as the optimal inflection point, achieving 100.00% precision (FP = 0). Observation units in the Core holding segment (q = 12 quarters) persis tently maintain their presence despite having non-registered status or revoked climate commitments (Commitment removed, 4.89%). We identify three primary mechanisms driving this mismatch: methodological scope divergence between MSCI’s holistic ESG risk ratings and SBTi’s absolute decarbonization targets, passive ETF rule-based replication inertia lacking automatic climate-revocation exclusion triggers, and transatlantic regulatory asymmetry. The findings underscore that current passive ESG index construction reflects proprietary financial risk management rather than verified real-world decarbonization.

title: The Licence as Burden: Regulatory Risk Reallocation, Foreign Capital, and the Debt Turn in Indian Fintech
affiliations: Shiv Nadar University

detail.title: The Licence as Burden: Regulatory Risk Reallocation, Foreign Capital, and the Debt Turn in Indian Fintech
detail.abstract: India’s September 2022 Digital Lending Guidelines shifted the credit risk of app-based consumer lending onto the balance sheets of licensed non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Partnership guarantees had offered licensed lenders credit-protected scale, letting investors underwrite them as platform-like growth assets; the Guidelines re-rated them into spread lenders whose growth consumes capital and bears first loss. Using 4,217 funding rounds by 1,490 Indian fintech firms over 2016–2026, with treatment coded from the RBI register as it stood one month before the event, we find licensed lenders’ probability of raising debt rose 15 percentage points — a near-doubling — concentrated in licensees without internal funding substitutes: young firms (+22 points) and, most sharply, those with no pre-event debt-market access (+29 points). Against matched comparables, the probability that any foreign equity investor participates in a licensed lender’s round falls 15–20 points, while intensity margins — share, lead roles, entry versus follow-on — are unchanged, treated firms’ equity-round rate does not fall relative to controls, and regulated categories without balance-sheet exposure show no debt turn. Foreign equity treated the licence as a burden rather than a certification; debt capital — domestic venturedebt funds and foreign impact-credit lenders — financed the balance sheets that new foreign equity would not.

title: Do Remittances Affect Healthy Diet Transformation in Nepal? Evidence From 1993 To 2023 Time-Series Data
affiliations: Tohoku University, Tohoku University and Tohoku University

detail.title: Do Remittances Affect Healthy Diet Transformation in Nepal? Evidence From 1993 To 2023 Time-Series Data
detail.abstract: Remittances significantly influence GDP-contributing sectors by stimulating household consumption and enhancing demand in the economy and are also an important source of household income; it is important to analyse whether remittances are supporting healthy diet transformation as the country is facing a critical dilemma of labor outmigration and sustainable food production. An autoregressive distributed lag model and an error correction model based on 31 years of time series data confirm that remittances are statistically significant and positively affect healthy diet transformation in the long run. Further, healthy diet production and imports of healthy diet positively influence healthy diet transformation. However, inflation and foreign agricultural assistance have negative impacts on healthy diet transformation. In the short run, only foreign agricultural assistance improves healthy diet transformation. The negative and significant error correction term indicates that 52% of short-term disequilibrium is corrected each year; if shocks lead to changes in dietary transformation, it will be corrected by 52 % next year. Remittances are important means of household consumption expenditure and improving living standards, it plays a critical role in supporting healthy dietary transformation, and this means remittances help to maintain qualitative dimensions of food security by ensuring diverse, nutritious, and balanced foods. Although remittances play a critical role in consumption expenditure, effective policy mechanisms are needed to channel remittances into productive investment rather than consumption only, which facilitates domestic production of a healthy diet and ensures nutritional adequacy and dietary diversity, which contributes to public health through affordability and accessibility.

title: The Double-Edged Sword of Commercialization: Food Security Implications Amid Heterogeneous Shocks in Malawi
affiliations: University of Malawi, University of Malawi, University of Malawi, University of Malawi and Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources

detail.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Commercialization: Food Security Implications Amid Heterogeneous Shocks in Malawi
detail.abstract: Malawi’s Vision 2063 identifies agricultural transformation as central to achieving economic growth and improved livelihoods. This study examines the causal impact of crop commercialization on household food security among smallholder farmers, with particular attention to the role of multiple shocks. Using data from the Fifth Integrated Household Survey (IHS5), the analysis applies quasi-experimental techniques to address both selection bias and endogeneity. Households engaged in commercialization are first matched with those below the commercialization threshold, after which an Instrumental Variable approach is employed to control for endogeneity. The main explanatory variables in the study were the Household Commercialization Index (HCI) and its interaction with the shock index. Food security was measured using the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS), Food Consumption Score (FCS), and Reduced Coping Strategies Index (rCSI). Results indicate that commercialization in the presence of multiple shocks exacerbates food insecurity, as households experience declines in their Food Consumption Score by 17.5 units and increases in the Reduced Coping Strategy Index by 35.5 units, reflecting greater reliance on coping strategies to buffer against hunger. Notably, this study also finds no evidence that commercialization alone improves HDDS, pointing to a trade-off between income gains and dietary quality. These findings highlight the need for policies that integrate market participation with resilience-building and nutrition-sensitive interventions to safeguard food security in shock-prone contexts. This study also suggests that while agricultural commercialization can offer economic benefits, its impact on food security is complex and context-dependent.

title: What Do Valuation Gaps Reveal? Market Valuation and Subsequent Corporate Adjustment
affiliations: and

detail.title: What Do Valuation Gaps Reveal? Market Valuation and Subsequent Corporate Adjustment
detail.abstract: Firms that own income-producing assets are routinely valued by capitalizing a current reported income measure at a fixed capitalization rate. We study the gap between a firm's market equity value and such a standardized benchmark. Because the capitalization rate is held fixed, the benchmark equals a capitalized income base less debt, so any revision to it divides exactly into an income-base component and a debt component. We use that identity. In a quarterly survivor panel of 176 United States real estate investment trusts from 2006 to 2019, a wider discount to the benchmark predicts subsequent deterioration in the income component and, working in the opposite direction, a substantial reduction in reported debt. A one standard deviation wider gap predicts directly reported debt falling by about 4% of assets over the following year. That response survives controls for operating information already observable, is not a crisis phenomenon, and does not depend on interpreting the income base.

title: Institutional Asymmetry in M&A Target Prediction: Machine Learning Evidence from Asia's Advanced and Emerging Markets
affiliations: and

detail.title: Institutional Asymmetry in M&A Target Prediction: Machine Learning Evidence from Asia's Advanced and Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: Despite an extensive M&A target-prediction literature in developed markets, the predictive content of established accounting and market signals across advanced and emerging institutional environments remains insufficiently quantified. This paper quantifies how predictive attribution shifts across these environments using firm-year panel data from ten Asian economies between 2000 and 2020. We estimate twelve machine learning models within a walk-forward panel design, with country and industry fixed effects entered via fold-wise residualization and emerging-market interaction terms that allow predictive associations to differ across regime groups. Three findings emerge. First, market-derived features account for approximately 34% more of the predictive signal in emerging markets than in advanced markets: twelve-month momentum extremes and changes in market-to-book valuations enter the emerging-market top ten, while no market-derived feature appears in the advanced-market top ten. The 34% gap is robust to leave-one-country-out re-estimation, split-sample subperiods, and alternative SHAP-ranking cutoffs. Second, the pooled XGBoost classifier achieves an out-of-sample area under the curve of 0.664 and outperforms the logistic baseline at the 1% level under paired DeLong tests, with three other tree ensembles also significantly improving on the baseline. Third, the upper tail of year-over-year changes in the debtto-assets ratio has the largest SHAP attribution in both regimes, and distributional extremes and volatility appear prominently in feature-attribution rankings while in-level central tendencies do not. The findings are consistent with an information-environment interpretation: where firm disclosures may be weaker, market signals receive additional predictive attribution.
