affiliations: NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Business and Management Science and NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Business and Management Science

detail.title: Regulatory Models and Pricing Mechanisms for District Heating in the Nordic Countries: Implications for Norway

publicationDetails.detailsText: NHH Dept. of Business and Management Science Discussion Paper No. 2026/9
publicationDetails.journalName: Norwegian School of Economics, Department of Business & Management Science Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: District heating (DH) is important for Nordic decarbonization and power-heat coordination, but its development differs markedly across the region, with Norway showing much lower DH penetration than Denmark, Sweden, and Finland. The analysis combines institutional comparison, a review of empirical pricing and modeling studies, and two stylized numerical case studies, to identify transferable lessons and suitable analytical tools for Norwegian policy reform aimed at supporting DH expansion. The results show that the main weakness of Norway's current electricity-indexed maximum-price rule lies not merely in the level of the cap, but in the instability of the benchmark and its weak alignment with the underlying cost structure and system value of DH. Greater electricity-price volatility can further amplify the mismatch between the electricity-linked cap and DH cost recovery, increasing downside revenue risk for DH companies. The representative-customer comparison shows that the current Norwegian regime exposes customers more directly to the market-linked price variation, while also making the tariff relatively more favorable for low-utilization customers, thereby increasing cost-recovery risks for DH companies. The Norwegian policy-counterfactual analysis shows that if Norway wishes to retain a maximum-price rule while revising its cap-setting method, using the cost of alternative heating technologies as a hard cap may be insufficient to ensure cost recovery under the Oslo calibration, whereas a Danish cost-recovery benchmark provides a more robust basis for long-run DH viability. Finally, the modeling review highlights the need for integrated, multi-model evaluation strategies to support evidence-based DH regulatory reform in Norway and other highly electrified energy systems.

title: The Legal Gray Zone of Proxy Voting Policies

detail.title: The Legal Gray Zone of Proxy Voting Policies

publicationDetails.journalName: Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Proxy voting policies are documents used by fiduciaries to outline how institutional shareholders use their voting power in corporate votes within their portfolio companies. These policies govern tens of trillions of dollars of assets under management (AUM) in the U.S. alone. 2 However, they occupy an unstable legal position. They are treated primarily as disclosure documents but operate as private regulatory instruments. This article develops the first doctrinal taxonomy of proxy voting policies, evaluating their functions as disclosure instruments, internal guidelines, contractual undertakings, and as private regulation. This analysis is supplemented by an empirical review of disclosures of proxy voting policies showing substantial heterogeneity in disclosure quality, presence of boilerplate language, reliance on proxy advisers, and uneven substantive guidance. 3 This article argues that current law under-regulates PVPs because it focuses on discretionary disclosure while ignoring their norm-setting powers. It proposes a tiered regulatory model based on proportionality and democratic legitimacy to enhance disclosure, compliance and accountability.

title: The Standardization Paradox: When Compliance Becomes a Predictable Vulnerability

detail.title: The Standardization Paradox: When Compliance Becomes a Predictable Vulnerability
detail.abstract: International management systems such as ISO and COSO have become global benchmarks for organizational governance, risk, and compliance. Their strength lies in standardization, documentation, and predictability. This paper introduces the concept of the Standardization Paradox - the condition where the very mechanisms designed to reduce risk become the primary vector of systemic attack. Drawing from three interdisciplinary lenses: financial trading, legal theory, and customary law, this paper demonstrates that highly structured and uniform systems are inherently readable and therefore exploitable. Through analysis of market microstructure, legal loophole exploitation, and ecological resilience theory, we argue that compliance does not equal security. The paper proposes a new model of Controlled Unpredictability and Deliberate Diversity as a necessary evolution beyond conventional compliance frameworks. [Adat]

title: Road Safety as a Test of Urban Governance: Why Uzbekistan's Problem is not Urbanization, but How it is Managed
affiliations: Center for Progressive Reforms

detail.title: Road Safety as a Test of Urban Governance: Why Uzbekistan's Problem is not Urbanization, but How it is Managed
detail.abstract:
This policy brief addresses Uzbekistan’s severe road-safety crisis, arguing that rising traffic fatalities are not an inevitable byproduct of rapid urbanization and motorization, but rather a structural governance failure. It examines how expanding mobility across urban corridors is currently undermined by three critical institutional vulnerabilities: bureaucratic fragmentation across enforcement and infrastructure agencies, the lack of an integrated interagency crash-data architecture, and transport investment models that do not enforce binding safety conditions during project appraisal and design. Drawing on national accident statistics and international reviews, the brief demonstrates that spending alone—without an integrated safety-governance framework—fails to yield proportional safety returns.

To overcome these challenges, the brief outlines a targeted, three-pillar reform package centered on establishing a Cabinet-level Road Safety Delivery Unit to align national targets, deploying a unified, geocoded interagency crash-intelligence database, and making rigorous road-safety audits a mandatory prerequisite for all infrastructure financing. Ultimately, the paper positions road-safety reform as a vital test of state capability and urban governance in Uzbekistan’s ongoing modernization strategy.

title: Proposed Amendments to the Co-Lead's Draft Protocol on the Taxation of Income from Cross-border Services, A/AC.298/CRP.33
affiliations: University of Nairobi

detail.title: Proposed Amendments to the Co-Lead's Draft Protocol on the Taxation of Income from Cross-border Services, A/AC.298/CRP.33
detail.abstract:
The fifth session of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee charged with elaborating the United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation was held in New York from 3 to 13 August 2026. Among the texts before delegations was the co-leads draft of the first Protocol, on the taxation of income derived from the provision of cross border services, which was presented at the session and engaged with in substance over the course of its meetings. The Committee on Fiscal Studies at the University of Nairobi, having read the draft closely, makes the observations recorded in this paper. We proceed from the position that the worth of the protocol will be determined less by the taxing rights it announces than by whether its machinery can be administered by the revenue authorities expected to apply it, above all those of African and other capital importing states whose position in the international tax order the Framework Convention process was convened to repair.

 

The submissions cover Article 1 on persons covered and the Protocol’s anti-abuse machinery, Article 2 on taxes covered and its interaction with relief under Article 10, Article 3 on the definition of royalties, Article 4 on dual residence, Article 5 on fees for services, Article 6 on income from automated digital services, Article 9 on taxation based on physical presence, and Article 10 on relief of double taxation. Each submission states the legal issue arising on the current text, explains the consequence that would follow in administration were the text left unamended, and proposes treaty language directed at resolving it.

title:
Mitigation Pathways for a Converging Global Polycrisis: 
Strategic Macroeconomic Interventions to Reduce Systemic Climate, Ecological, and Financial Risk

detail.title:
Mitigation Pathways for a Converging Global Polycrisis: 
Strategic Macroeconomic Interventions to Reduce Systemic Climate, Ecological, and Financial Risk
detail.abstract:
The Global Polycrisis Report examines how interacting systemic stresses—climate instability, geopolitical fragmentation, technological disruption, financial volatility, and resource constraints—are converging to produce compounding global risks. The report synthesizes cross‑sector evidence to map how these crises reinforce one another through feedback loops, tipping dynamics, and institutional vulnerabilities. It identifies the most probable escalation pathways over the next decade and evaluates mitigation strategies capable of reducing systemic fragility rather than addressing isolated symptoms.

Using integrated assessment models, network‑risk analysis, and scenario simulations, the report finds that coordination failures, energy‑system transitions, and supply‑chain chokepoints are the dominant drivers of cascading instability. However, it also highlights leverage points—such as accelerated clean‑energy deployment, resilient infrastructure investment, digital‑governance reforms, and cooperative economic frameworks—that can meaningfully reduce global exposure to synchronized shocks.

The report concludes that effective mitigation requires shifting from crisis‑specific interventions to whole‑system resilience strategies, emphasizing adaptive governance, distributed redundancy, and long‑term capacity building. These pathways offer a viable route to stabilizing global systems under conditions of persistent uncertainty and accelerating change.

title: Distinguishing Market Risk from Platform Risk in Digital Gold: A Conceptual Trust-infrastructure Framework

detail.title: Distinguishing Market Risk from Platform Risk in Digital Gold: A Conceptual Trust-infrastructure Framework
detail.abstract: Digital gold platforms have lowered the practical barriers to buying, holding, and redeeming gold, yet retail users continue to perceive them as risky even when interfaces are mature and prices are competitive. This paper argues that persistent distrust is not primarily a usability or price-discovery problem but a trust-infrastructure problem rooted in information asymmetry between platforms and users. The central analytical contribution is the explicit decomposition of a user’s total exposure into two conceptually distinct components: market risk (gold-price volatility, which no platform can remove) and platform risk (custody design, reconciliation, redemption terms, security, and operational resilience, which platforms can reduce through governance and disclosure). Building on the economics of information asymmetry, the organizational-trust literature, and industry custody standards, the paper develops a five-dimension conceptual framework — asset backing, transparency, redeemability, security, and operational resilience — for characterizing the credibility of digital-gold arrangements, and links each dimension to observable, verifiable evidence. The paper’s contribution is conceptual and definitional rather than empirical: it clarifies terminology (allocated, unallocated, pooled, and price-linked exposure), formalizes the market-versus-platform distinction, and proposes a structured set of criteria that can be operationalized in future empirical work. Limitations and an agenda for empirical validation are discussed.

title: Historical Evolution of Auctions and Public Sales: Delegated Agent of Public Power
affiliations: University of Curitiba - Curitiba School of Law, UNICURITIBA and

detail.title: Historical Evolution of Auctions and Public Sales: Delegated Agent of Public Power

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The second author was a named petitioner, together with the National Association of Judicial Auctioneers, in the administrative control proceeding discussed in Part VII, and authored the legal opinion that supported it. He serves as President of the National Association of Judicial Auctioneers and of the São Paulo State Auctioneers' Union, professional bodies whose members benefit from the rule under discussion. The account of the proceeding rests on the published decisions rather than on the author's own recollection.

detail.abstract: Objective. This article analyses the historical evolution of auctions from their origins in Antiquity to their contemporary configuration in Brazil as a delegated public function. The legal analysis addresses the nature of the delegation of public function to the auctioneer, its reception by the current constitutional order, and the public faith attaching to the office. The adaptation of the activity to the digital era is examined critically. Methodology. Deductive method, by historical-descriptive, bibliographic and documentary approach, based on analysis of primary and secondary sources. Results and contribution. The study shows how the auction consolidated as an instrument of social and economic relevance, culminating in Brazilian regulation through Decree-Law No. 21,981 of 19 October 1932. Following the administrative control proceeding decided by the National Council of Justice in 2021 and the Supreme Federal Court's refusal to disturb it in 2023, it is concluded that conducting a judicial auction is a public function that cannot be delegated to private companies. Technology does not eliminate but rather reinforces the need for the auctioneer as an agent endowed with public faith. 2

title: Fiscal Rigidities and their Effects in Ghana: What Should the Government Do?
affiliations: Institute for Fiscal Studies, Ghana

detail.title: Fiscal Rigidities and their Effects in Ghana: What Should the Government Do?
detail.abstract: In spite of the fact that many reasons are usually used to justify the presence of fiscal rigidities, they have been found to pose serious fiscal and macroeconomic difficulties to some countries, particularly those in Latin America, since they make governments lose the discretion and flexibility to use fiscal policy to address emerging fiscal and macroeconomic challenges. Yet, fiscal rigidities have not received the needed attention in Africa in terms of research. We therefore study in this paper fiscal rigidities and their fiscal and macroeconomic effects in Ghana. We find that fiscal rigidities have significant negative effects on Ghana’s fiscal and macroeconomic outcomes. Thus, high degree of fiscal rigidity as measured by the size of total rigid expenditure relative to total revenue and grants has historically led to very poor fiscal and macroeconomic outcomes in Ghana, and vice versa. In fact, we find that the fiscal and macroeconomic difficulties the country is currently going through are largely due to fiscal rigidities that have now reached alarming proportions, which are comparable only to the state in which the country found itself prior to the HIPC debt reliefs. We have therefore provided in this paper a number of recommendations that, we believe, can reduce the degree of rigidity in the country’s budget in order to reverse the current poor fiscal and macroeconomic performances.

title: An Analytical Study of the "Sudan First" Vision
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title: An Analytical Study of the "Sudan First" Vision

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I am a researcher and that is the biggest problem facing my country, Sudan
declarations.ethicsApproval: There is no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Funding

detail.abstract: The paper presents a comprehensive theoretical-applied framework for post-conflict state reconstruction in Sudan, grounded in the "Sudan First" vision, which proposes a bottomup approach to state-building. The study argues that sustainable political stability cannot be achieved through top-down governmental formation alone, but rather through ascending legitimacy produced from the social base to the institutional apex, with a clear functional separation between political competition and state administration. Drawing on legitimacy theory, demographic transition theory, institutionalism, social contract theory, and comparative post-conflict reconstruction literature, the paper develops a multi-stage roadmap comprising four sequential phases: (1) crisis management and grassroots organization, (2) recovery and institutional preparation, (3) state-building and democratic transition, and (4) consolidation and sustainable development. The framework integrates mechanisms for combating corruption through community oversight, countering terrorism through local peacekeeping forces and security sector reform, and addressing the demographic youth bulge through productive employment and livelihood empowerment. The analysis demonstrates that effective state reconstruction requires the integration of security, development, and justice within a unified sequence that addresses the root causes of conflict rather than merely managing its symptoms. The paper contributes to the growing literature on post-conflict reconstruction by providing an operational architecture for bottom-up legitimacy production in fragile state contexts.

title: Revenue Earmarking in Ghana: Management and Performance Issues
affiliations: Institute for Fiscal Studies, Ghana

detail.title: Revenue Earmarking in Ghana: Management and Performance Issues
detail.abstract: Although revenue earmarking was seldom used in Ghana before the fourth republic, it has now become a common fiscal practice. Specifically, while only two formal earmarking arrangements existed in the country before the fourth republic, there are currently 11 arrangements of revenue earmarking with one more in the pipeline.  Because earmarking currently consumes a large chunk of the country’s fiscal resources with about 35% of total revenue and grants earmarked in 2013, ensuring effective management of the various earmarked funds is an important component of the country’s quest for effective fiscal management. This paper examines how effectively the various earmarked funds have been managed and how they have performed. The paper finds that the earmarked funds in Ghana face entrenched management challenges, which, with the exception of a handful, have led to poor performance of the funds. The usefulness of revenue earmarking in Ghana is therefore undermined. In addition to recommending against the establishment of new earmarked funds in Ghana unless they are found to be essential, the paper provides a number of recommendations as to how best the management challenges can be addressed in order to improve the performance of the existing earmarked funds to justify their continuous existence.

title: Mandatory Rules and International Arbitration: Party Autonomy, Overriding Mandatory Laws and the Enforceability of Awards
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Mandatory Rules and International Arbitration: Party Autonomy, Overriding Mandatory Laws and the Enforceability of Awards
detail.abstract: International commercial arbitration is founded on party autonomy, but commercial disputes increasingly engage regulatory rules that states regard as non-waivable. Competition law, anticorruption rules, sanctions, foreign-exchange controls, agency protections and other regulatory statutes may claim application even when the parties have chosen a different substantive law. The central difficulty is that arbitral tribunals lack a single forum conflict rule equivalent to that of a national court, while an award that disregards a sufficiently important norm may later confront annulment or enforcement objections. This article argues that the problem cannot be solved either by treating party autonomy as absolute or by allowing every self-described mandatory rule to override the parties' choice. It distinguishes ordinary mandatory provisions, overriding mandatory rules and international public policy, and uses comparative analysis of European Union conflict law, United States jurisprudence, English enforcement doctrine and French public-policy review. The article proposes a calibrated mandatory-rules method based on four inquiries: the rule's genuine overriding claim, the juridical proximity between the regulating state and the transaction, the transnational legitimacy of the protected interest, and the consequences for the award's enforceability, subject throughout to procedural fairness. This framework preserves party autonomy as the starting point while recognising that arbitral legitimacy depends on reasoned engagement with regulatory norms whose application is sufficiently connected, legitimate and consequential.

title: Engineering Organizational Negotiation Representations: An Architecture for Human and AI Reasoning

detail.title: Engineering Organizational Negotiation Representations: An Architecture for Human and AI Reasoning
detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly use AI to support complex negotiations, but most current approaches focus on improving AI generated analysis rather than the organizational representations over which humans and AI jointly reason. The preceding paper argued that organizations can benefit from such explicit representations; this paper addresses the corresponding engineering question: how they can be constructed in the age of large language models. The central argument is that AI changes the economics of representation, not the organizational need for it. Earlier knowledge-based systems required substantial representational structure to be modeled explicitly before computational reasoning could begin; contemporary AI can infer much of that structure dynamically from lightly structured information, substantially reducing the cost of construction and maintenance. AI can readily generate a common representation format. It does not automatically generate a common organizational truth. The paper proposes a three layer architecture: a comprehensive project repository preserving organizational evidence, a persistent organizational representation capturing current understanding, and dynamically generated analytical representations for specific reasoning tasks. Building on this architecture, a Human and AI reasoning lifecycle combines AI supported analysis and representational maintenance with human organizational judgment and commitment. The architecture governs how AI contributions become part of the organization's accepted representation rather than restricting the scope of AI supported reasoning. The architecture is expected to improve negotiation preparation and organizational decision making through better alignment, broader exploration of alternatives, less repeated reconstruction of project context, and a more stable basis for organizational learning. Transparency, governance and traceability emerge largely from the representational structure rather than as separate downstream controls.

title: When the Test Fails Before the Data Arrives: A Unified Taxonomy of Statistical Pitfalls in Industry Experimentation

detail.title: When the Test Fails Before the Data Arrives: A Unified Taxonomy of Statistical Pitfalls in Industry Experimentation
detail.abstract: Online controlled experiments have become the dominant empirical tool for decision-making across technology platforms, financial institutions, and quantitative investment firms. Yet the growing institutional reliance on A/B testing coexists with a persistent and underappreciated set of statistical failure modes that are rarely catalogued in a unified framework. This paper identifies three foundational pitfalls that together account for the majority of invalid inferences drawn from industry experimentation: (1) optional-stopping inflation, the systematic elevation of false-positive rates when experiments are monitored continuously without corrected decision boundaries; (2) interference bias, the violation of the Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption in networked, marketplace, and portfolio environments that renders naive treatment-effect estimates meaningless; and (3) selection bias under multiple testing, the inflation of apparent performance when the reported result is the best of many trials without correction for the search process. These pitfalls are not independent curiosities; they share a common mathematical structure rooted in the misapplication of fixed-sample frequentist inference to settings that violate its foundational assumptions. The paper demonstrates this structure analytically and then traces how each pitfall manifests distinctively across three industry contexts: large-scale product experimentation in technology firms, credit and pricing experiments in retail banking and fintech, and strategy evaluation in quantitative hedge funds. The cross-industry comparison reveals that the severity of each pitfall is determined primarily by the incentive structure of the institution and the dependence structure of the units under study, not by the sophistication of the analytical team. Remedies are discussed for each context, with particular attention to sequential testing methods, clusterrandomized designs, and the deflated Sharpe ratio as domain-specific corrections. The paper closes by arguing that the appropriate response is not a collection of ad hoc fixes but a pre-registration discipline that forces institutions to specify stopping rules, randomization units, and primary endpoints before data are observed.

title: Green Logistics Efficiency across Egyptian Industrial Regions: A DEA Sensitivity Analysis

detail.title: Green Logistics Efficiency across Egyptian Industrial Regions: A DEA Sensitivity Analysis
detail.abstract: This study develops a transparent data envelopment analysis (DEA) workflow for examining green logistics efficiency across Egyptian industrial regions. Eighteen named regions were represented by a fully synthetic input-output matrix containing energy, infrastructure, logistics labor, emissions burden, service output, recovery output, and reliability. The input-oriented model produced a mean efficiency score of 0.881, a median of 0.940, and seven frontier units; the lowest score was 0.585. A ±10% perturbation to the emissions input left mean efficiency unchanged at three decimals, indicating aggregate stability under that narrow test while not establishing stability for every unit or alternative specification. The study demonstrates how efficiency, environmental burden, and service output can be assessed jointly and why sensitivity analysis should accompany regional comparisons. Because every input and output is synthetic, the results validate the method and reporting pipeline rather than rank actual Egyptian regions.

title: Res Judicata and Issue Estoppel in International Arbitration: Finality, Inconsistent Awards and the Limits of Arbitral Jurisdiction
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Res Judicata and Issue Estoppel in International Arbitration: Finality, Inconsistent Awards and the Limits of Arbitral Jurisdiction
detail.abstract: International arbitration depends on finality, yet its transnational character makes the law of preclusion unusually unstable. A prior award may be invoked before a second tribunal; a court judgment may determine an issue later raised in arbitration; and a seat court's decision on award validity may reappear before an enforcement court in another jurisdiction. The resulting questions are often described under the broad label res judicata, but the relevant doctrines-claim preclusion, issue estoppel, abuse of process and transnational issue estoppel-do not operate identically across legal systems. This article argues that international arbitration should treat preclusion principally as a rule of admissibility and finality rather than jurisdiction. Comparative analysis of England and Wales, Singapore and France shows why that characterisation matters: an erroneous preclusion ruling will ordinarily be an error on the merits, not an excess of jurisdiction, while the enforcing court retains distinct Convention-based controls. The article further argues that transnational issue estoppel can reduce repetitive challenges to award validity, but only where the prior decision is genuinely final and conclusive, the parties and issue coincide, and recognition would not offend forum public policy or procedural justice. It proposes a five-stage preclusion protocol designed to reconcile finality, party autonomy, legal diversity and the prevention of inconsistent arbitral and judicial outcomes.

title: Utilizing Immersive Virtual Reality (IVR) in Legal Education: Voice from Bangladesh
affiliations: and University of North Dakota

detail.title: Utilizing Immersive Virtual Reality (IVR) in Legal Education: Voice from Bangladesh
detail.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) offers immense potential to revolutionize legal education in Bangladesh, where its applications remain limited. Using a mixed-methods approach, a longitudinal survey was conducted on law faculty members from various universities to explore their perceptions and importance of VR integration in law curricula. The survey collected both quantitative and qualitative data, with 59 eligible responses analyzed. Findings indicate overwhelmingly positive attitudes toward VR's capacity to enhance student engagement, memory retention, and comprehension of abstract legal concepts (mean score: 4.0+). Faculty members also recognized the value of VR in providing immersive courtroom simulations, allowing students to develop practical skills in a risk-free environment. The study reveals that VR has the potential to transform legal education by fostering experiential learning, deeper understanding, and skill-building opportunities.

title: Technical, Regulatory, and Financial Conditions for Bankable Water Reuse Projects: A Multiple Case Study of AI Data Center Cooling Infrastructure

detail.title: Technical, Regulatory, and Financial Conditions for Bankable Water Reuse Projects: A Multiple Case Study of AI Data Center Cooling Infrastructure
detail.abstract: This study examines the conditions under which urban water reuse can become bankable cooling infrastructure for AI data centers. Using Microsoft-Quincy as the benchmark case and Google Douglas County and Amazon Web Services as comparative cases, it applies a fit-forpurpose framework across three interdependent dimensions: technical, regulatory, and financial. Technical fit concerns water quality, cooling-system compatibility, supply reliability, monitoring, backup capacity, and residuals management. Regulatory fit concerns permitted end use, discharge requirements, institutional authority, public acceptance, and governance. Financial fit concerns capital and operating costs, tariff design, long-term offtake, creditworthy demand, cashflow certainty, and risk allocation. The study argues that no dimension is sufficient independently. Bankability emerges when all three are aligned strongly enough to convert reclaimed water from a technically possible resource into a reliable utility service with recoverable costs and manageable long-term risks.

title: Who Pivots after Failure? Psychological Capital Change, Performance Feedback, and Market Repositioning in Crowdfunding
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong -Liverpool University, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) - School of Management, Shenzhen University and Shenzhen University

detail.title: Who Pivots after Failure? Psychological Capital Change, Performance Feedback, and Market Repositioning in Crowdfunding
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurial pivoting—a strategic change in venture direction—is central to entrepreneurship research, yet its person-side antecedents remain unexplored. We study how the psychological trajectory founders carry out of failure shapes whether they reposition or return to the old market. Drawing on PsyCap and performance feedback research, we propose an inverted U-shaped relationship between PsyCap change across a failure and the likelihood of a market positioning pivot: depleted founders lack the energy to change course; exuberant founders see no need to change. We further propose that performance feedback from the failed venture moderates this relationship in opposite ways: the funding ratio steepens the curve; fundraising speed flattens it. Analyses of 445 matched failed follow-up Kickstarter campaign pairs support the inverted U and the moderating role of speed; the ratio moderation is marginal. We reconcile threat-rigidity and prospect-theory accounts of post-failure change, showing that psychological recovery helps strategic change only in moderation.

title: Formalizations of Bicchieri's Social Norm Theory in Agent-Based Models: A Qualitative Systematic Literature Review
affiliations: , Hamburg University of Technology and Hamburg University of Technology

detail.title: Formalizations of Bicchieri's Social Norm Theory in Agent-Based Models: A Qualitative Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: Cristina Bicchieri’s Social Norm Theory presents a detailed behavioral account of how social expectations shape individual decisions and, consequently, can generate desirable collective patterns such as saving energy. Agent-based models (ABMs) have become a commonly used tool for studying how these micro-level decisions generate macro-level norm dynamics. However, translating social science theories into ABMs typically requires substantial interpretation of the theory as well as consideration of the application context. As a result, existing translations may differ in their formalizations, vary widely across disciplines, and yield diverging simulation outcomes. Therefore, we conducted a qualitative systematic literature review (not registered, given its exploratory nature), screening 878 publications extracted from Scopus and Google Scholar, to identify and compare options for how Bicchieri’s theory can be formalized in ABMs. In this process, we examined formalization options of core concepts of Bicchieri’s theory (i.e., reference networks, social expectations, personal normative beliefs, and norm sensitivity) as well as agents’ decision-making. Across the identified 24 publications – focusing on studies explicitly referencing Bicchieri’s work – we synthesized and documented recurring patterns in formalization options alongside substantial variation. Because standard risk-of-bias tools are not designed for qualitative synthesis of formalization choices, we adapted an approach informed by Cochrane RoB 2 and ROBIS to assess our main findings, confirming that our main outcomes remain largely robust. Our results offer a structured catalog of formalization options that modelers can reuse and combine when implementing Bicchieri’s theory. We also identify several avenues for future research, including opportunities to advance empirical calibration practices. To strengthen cross-study comparability and foster cumulative model development, we suggest improving the traceability between theoretical constructs and formalizations, along with promoting greater reuse of proven formalizations.

title: Identification and Efficient Estimation of Latent Consideration Sets via Partial Observation
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School, University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School

detail.title: Identification and Efficient Estimation of Latent Consideration Sets via Partial Observation
detail.abstract: We study the identification and efficient estimation of consider-then-choose (CTC) models when latent consideration sets are partially observed through noisy heatmap sensors. We show that joint sales and heatmap data suffice for point identification without exclusion restrictions, and we develop a tractable, globally concave two-step estimator. Our contributions are fourfold: (i) an identification proof from joint sales and heatmap data; (ii) a computationally efficient two-step estimator in which both stages solve globally concave optimization problems, reducing the computational cost from exponential to linear in the number of products via a Jensen surrogate; (iii) an information-theoretic characterization based on Louis' missing-information principle, showing that Fisher information increases monotonically with sensor precision; and (iv) decision-regret bounds that decompose into variance and bias components, quantifying the economic value of improved sensor accuracy. Together, these results establish a unified framework linking identification, computational tractability, and information efficiency in models with latent consideration.

title: Decoupling Grid Triggers from Trade Decisions: A Constrained Event-Driven Reinforcement Learning Architecture for ETF Trading

detail.title: Decoupling Grid Triggers from Trade Decisions: A Constrained Event-Driven Reinforcement Learning Architecture for ETF Trading

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses historical market data and does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Grid trading normally converts every boundary crossing into an order, coupling event detection with execution. This study introduces Event-Driven Geometric Moving Grid Trading (EDGMGT), an architecture that retains the geometric grid as an auditable event generator while assigning post-trigger execution to a constrained policy. At each event, maskable proximal policy optimization (MaskablePPO) selects Buy, Sell, or Hold after removing actions that violate grid direction, cash, inventory, or position limits. The empirical study uses minute-level Bank exchange-traded fund (ETF) data from 2018 to 2023 with chronological training, validation, and testing. On a common 242-day test calendar, the average-true-range anchor configuration records an annualized return of 1.50%, a Sharpe ratio of 0.36, and maximum drawdown of 3.17%, compared with -0.79%, -0.08, and 6.10% for the mechanical grid. All 994 observed Hold actions occur while the direction-consistent trade remains feasible. Random feasible-action and exposure-matched diagnostics link the downside result to a state-dependent exposure path, while paired block bootstraps preserve the drawdown reduction against mechanical execution. EDGMGT shows how transparent financial rules can define decision events while a learned, constraint-aware layer determines execution.

title: Algorithmic Dispatch vs. Order Grabbing: Experimental Evidence from an On-demand Delivery Platform
affiliations: and The Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Algorithmic Dispatch vs. Order Grabbing: Experimental Evidence from an On-demand Delivery Platform
detail.abstract: Dispatch design determines who controls task assignment on digital labor platforms. Centralized algorithms can improve system-wide coordination and curb strategic selection, but may also suppress workers' private local knowledge. We study this trade-off in a matched two-city field experiment with a large Chinese on-demand delivery platform. One city shifted from decentralized courier order grabbing to centralized algorithmic dispatch, while the comparison city retained order grabbing. Using 1.94 million orders and a difference-indifferences design, we find that centralized dispatch reduces fulfillment time by 7.1% and the probability of late delivery by 1.53 percentage points, an 18.4% decline relative to the pretreatment mean. Our heterogeneity analysis along order distance, an important operational characteristic in on-demand delivery, shows that these performance gains are substantially larger for short-distance orders than for long-distance orders. The gains arise primarily from shorter matching and pickup stages: algorithmic dispatch reduces courier-to-pickup distance but does not affect merchant-to-customer distance, and its benefits are larger during peak demand. Centralization also produces greater improvements for low-earning-efficiency orders, while couriers with stronger prior cherry-picking tendencies benefit less, consistent with reduced strategic sorting. Yet more experienced couriers also benefit less, suggesting that centralized assignment partly displaces valuable local knowledge. These findings characterize dispatch architecture as a governance choice that trades off system-level coordination and selection control against worker-level private information. Rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all approach, platforms should dynamically balance algorithmic dispatch and order grabbing according to market conditions, such as market thickness and peak demand periods, while preserving the value of courier-level private knowledge and discretion.

title: Human Capital Pipelines -Antecedents and Consequences
affiliations: Stockton University

detail.title: Human Capital Pipelines -Antecedents and Consequences
detail.abstract: Purpose The paper aims to discuss the concept of human capital pipelines and explain how pipelines originate and the consequences of pipeline-based hiring in terms of labor market uncertainty, job embeddedness, social ties, homosocial reproduction, employee referrals, and turnover intent. Design/methodology/approach The author provides a viewpoint grounded on a review of recent research regarding human capital pipelines. Findings This paper aims at further developing our understanding of human capital pipelines and the implications of such practices. The author points out both the positive and negative aspects of pipeline-based hiring, with the hope that human resource practitioners and mangers will adopt such practices based on the organization's strategic needs. Originality/value To date, very little conceptual and/or empirical work has been carried out on pipeline-based hiring. In organizations, it is important to understand how repeated hiring from labor sources can reduce labor market uncertainty regarding a job seeker's quality and potential productivity. However, it is also crucial to appreciate that such practices may have important pre and post hire implications for organizations and employees alike.

title: The Dynamic Role of Fit in Human Capital Pipelines: A Co-evolutionary Perspective
affiliations: Stockton University

detail.title: The Dynamic Role of Fit in Human Capital Pipelines: A Co-evolutionary Perspective
detail.abstract: Purpose This paper seeks to outline the crucial role of "fit" in the development and maintenance of human capital pipelines. It presents the argument that "fit" is not a static concept but rather a dynamic, co-evolutionary process, where the effectiveness of the pipeline is determined by the continuous and reciprocal alignment of the evolving aspirations of both individuals and organizations. Design/methodology/approach This perspective synthesizes concepts from three key areas: Person-Environment fit theory, the Resource-Based View of the firm, and organizational aspiration theory. This paper offers a refined framework that highlights the strategic necessity of managing "fit" as a continuous, dynamic process rather than a one-time, static event. This approach provides a more nuanced understanding of how organizations and individuals can achieve sustained alignment. Findings The paper elaborates on how the pursuit of performance aspirations and competitive tiering drives organizational aspirations, which in turn shapes talent acquisition strategies. It also details how individual aspirations, such as career aspirations and a desire for value alignment, guide a job seeker's behavior. The dynamic interplay between these two sets of aspirations is shown to be the primary driver of a sustainable fit. The paper also discusses the consequences of aspiration congruence and misalignment, including the central paradox of organizational cohesion versus the need for innovation. Originality/value To date, very little conceptual work has integrated the concepts of fit and aspirations in the context of human capital pipelines. This paper offers a multi-dimensional framework that provides a novel understanding of these complex relationships, serving as a valuable theoretical and practical guide for researchers and practitioners alike.

title:
Why GCCs Cannot Become Strategic Unless Accountability and Authority Evolve Together 
A Practitioner's Perspective from HR Shared Services and Global Business Services

detail.title:
Why GCCs Cannot Become Strategic Unless Accountability and Authority Evolve Together 
A Practitioner's Perspective from HR Shared Services and Global Business Services

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no known financial, professional, or personal conflicts of interest that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or identifiable personal data. Therefore, ethics committee approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was self-funded by the authors.

detail.abstract: For more than two decades I have helped build, run, and transform Global Capability Centers and HR Shared Services organizations across Asia Pacific, Europe, and North America. In almost every case, the ambition stated at the outset was the same. The center was meant to move beyond cost savings and become a strategic partner to the business. Many centers achieve this, and I have seen it done well. Where the transition stalls, I argue in this paper that the reason is usually structural, and it sits in the operating model designed at headquarters rather than in the talent, technology, or intent of the center itself. When a parent organization increases what a center is accountable for without granting the matching authority to act, it creates a gap that limits value on both sides. Leaders are asked to own transformation, quality, and business results, while the decision rights over budget, hiring, process design, technology, and vendor selection remain elsewhere. Left unaddressed, this mismatch shows up as slower progress, difficulty retaining senior leaders, and a ceiling on value that operational excellence alone cannot lift. Drawing on my direct experience running HR Shared Services and payroll operations, alongside published industry research on the GCC sector, I set out how accountability and authority drift apart, why the gap is common, and how to close it. I then offer a maturity view and a practical, phased approach for advancing the two together. The central point is constructive and simple. When a center is given both the responsibility for an outcome and the authority to shape it, it becomes a genuine strategic partner. Aligning the two is a design choice well within the reach of any organization willing to make it.

title: Collective Engagement as A Cultural Property and the Sensemaking Processes for Its Formation

detail.title: Collective Engagement as A Cultural Property and the Sensemaking Processes for Its Formation
detail.abstract: Organizational behavior as engagement or commitment or involvement has been extensively studied, especially as a form of individual attitude. Less studied has been engagement as a cultural property of an organization. This article analyzes the sensemaking processes that determine the construction of collective engagement as a cultural property starting from the perceptions and expectations that people consolidate in their work experiences. The problem of influencing organizational culture remains an open problem in the exercise of leadership at all levels, especially in the face of the need to promote innovation. The way to promote the sharing of cultural contents remains problematic. In the analyzes aimed at measuring culture, the lack of convergence of responses often emerges, e.g. regarding the level of engagement of the staff. A multilevel analysis, based on data collected in 100 organizations, helps to describe the phenomena of conferring meaning that influence these processes. The data show that in most organizations the degree of sharing of meanings is rather low. At the same time, these data highlight the moderating effect that the relational context can exert in fostering an increase in collective engagement, as a concrete way in which organizational culture manifests itself.

title: The Impact of Immigrant Talent on Global Product Strategy
affiliations: Brown University, University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School

detail.title: The Impact of Immigrant Talent on Global Product Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper examines how skilled immigrants hired at headquarters (HQ), an increasingly important source of talent for firms, shape two key aspects of global product strategy: where to offer products and the balance between standardization versus local adaptation of those products. We assemble a unique dataset by linking 204,129 consumer packaged goods launched in 84 countries by 470 U.S.-based firms from Mintel GNPD to USCIS microdata on all H-1B workers hired by those firms. We develop an instrument that isolates random variation in firms' ability to obtain workers of specific nationalities and use NLP techniques to create a novel adaptation-standardization index at the product level. We find that the arrival of workers from a given country at HQ increases product launches in that country. This effect is weaker when the firm already has a subsidiary in the focal country but stronger when it has prior experience launching products in that country. The adaptation-standardization balance depends on the presence of a subsidiary: immigrants at HQ lead products to become more locally adapted if a subsidiary is not present in their home country, but more globally standardized if a subsidiary is present. Immigrants also tilt products towards local adaptation if the firm lacks prior product launch experience in the focal country. Our study demonstrates how the knowledge brought by immigrant talent at HQ works in tandem with the firm's governance structure and its marketspecific capabilities to determine global product strategy.

title: Historical Aspects of Global Communication: Trade, Religion, Empire, Diplomacy, and Technology in the Formation of Interconnected Worlds

detail.title: Historical Aspects of Global Communication: Trade, Religion, Empire, Diplomacy, and Technology in the Formation of Interconnected Worlds
detail.abstract: This article examines historical aspects of global communication as a long civilizational process shaped by mobility, diplomacy, trade, religion, empire, colonization, slavery, and technology. Global communication did not begin with modern media systems. Its foundations were laid much earlier through the movement of peoples, the organization of trade, the spread of belief, the conduct of diplomacy, the exercise of imperial rule, and the invention of increasingly powerful means of transmitting messages across distance. Communication developed not only as a means of sharing information, but also as a mechanism of negotiation, recognition, secrecy, authority, persuasion, legal ordering, coercion, and strategic restraint. Diplomacy formed one of its most durable structures because rulers, communities, kingdoms, empires, and later states repeatedly depended on organized communication to negotiate peace, alliance, tribute, trade, coexistence, and survival. Exploration and discovery broadened geographical awareness and brought distant worlds into closer contact with one another. Trade enhanced contacts regularly beyond borders and was materialized, spoken loudly, and was so necessary and demanding. Christianity created transregional networks of doctrine, conduct, and communal belonging. Illyricum and Macedonia occupied an important place within the Roman-apostolic horizon as historically active regional spaces of movement, integration, and transmission. Colonization and slavery reordered communication through command, classification, labor control, legal imposition, and unequal representation. Communication technologies, from writing to telegraphy, radio, telephony, and later digital systems, accelerated the reach and force of communication across the world. Modern global communication systems, therefore, rest upon older historical formations through which societies negotiated exchange, belief, hierarchy, dependency, and conflict in the making of increasingly interconnected worlds.

title: Channel-Aware Hierarchical Demand Forecasting for Omnichannel Supply Chains: Regime-Conditional Reconciliation of E-Commerce and Store Demand Signals

detail.title: Channel-Aware Hierarchical Demand Forecasting for Omnichannel Supply Chains: Regime-Conditional Reconciliation of E-Commerce and Store Demand Signals
detail.abstract: Omnichannel retailers must produce demand forecasts that are simultaneously accurate and coherent across a hierarchy that crosses a product taxonomy with a sales-channel dimension. Existing forecast reconciliation methods estimate a single, unconditional covariance matrix of base-forecast errors, an assumption that we show is badly violated in omnichannel data. Using 1034 days of transaction records from a retail chain that operates 57 physical stores and two e-commerce channels over the same product catalogue, we document three properties that break static reconciliation: (i) online demand grows from 0.65% to 9.07% of units while store volume falls by 53%, so aggregation weights are non-stationary; (ii) base-forecast error variances follow a steep power law in the conditional mean (median Taylor exponent κ = 1.63) and are 2.66 times larger on demand-shock days; and (iii) the cross-channel error correlation structure differs measurably between calm and shock regimes. We propose CHARM, a channel-aware reconciliation method with three components: a total-and-share parameterisation that forecasts the cross-channel group total and the online share instead of the two channel series separately; a forecast-conditional heteroscedastic scale built from a Taylor power law; and a two-regime correlation mixture with hierarchical shrinkage, weighted by a learned shock probability. CHARM preserves coherence and unbiasedness for any positive-definite conditional covariance. On a 43-origin rolling evaluation it reduces mean RMSSE by 2.6% and MASE by 5.5% relative to MinT with shrinkage, by 8.1% on shock days, and cuts downstream order-upto inventory cost by 7.7%. Ablations confirm that each component contributes, and a cross-domain study on Australian retail turnover shows the method does not degrade where its conditioning signals are uninformative.

title: Strategic use of Social Media to Screen Job Applicants – a Review of the Benefits, Concerns and Best Practices
affiliations: Stockton University

detail.title: Strategic use of Social Media to Screen Job Applicants – a Review of the Benefits, Concerns and Best Practices
detail.abstract: Purpose This paper examines the role of social media in screening job seekers. As social media sites have gained popularity in recent times, organizations are able to access large amounts of professional and personal information of job applicants. This information is used primarily to narrow the applicant pool, but concerns exist regarding the appropriateness of using such practices. The author identifies several best practices that can increase the effectiveness and reliability of using social media as a source of applicant data. Design/methodology/approach The author reviewed relevant literature and research on the use of social media websites to screen applicants, identifying the benefits of such practices, along with its costs. Findings This paper aims at further developing our understanding of strategically using social media for applicant screening purposes and the implications of such practices. The author points out both the positive and negative aspects of using social media as a screening tool, with the hope that practitioners will use the information from job seekers’ social media pages in an unbiased and non-discriminatory manner. Originality/value This paper provides guidelines regarding appropriate utilization of social media as a screening tool as part of an organization’s recruitment and selection process.

title: Ephemeral Promises of Happiness: Coming Out in the Australian Accounting Profession into the Late 2010s
affiliations: The University of Sydney and

detail.title: Ephemeral Promises of Happiness: Coming Out in the Australian Accounting Profession into the Late 2010s
detail.abstract: This interview-based study explores how shifting promises of happiness impact on LGBTIQ+ individuals within the workplace. Our study situates within the “Big 4” Australian professional service firms at a time of significant political change, centered around the legislating of marriage equality in 2017. Together with statements of support issued by each of these firms, these moves offered an increasing sense that secure promises of happiness were now offered to “out” LGBTIQ+ staff. A shifting of hetero-cis normativities was suggested, offering some sense of greater safety, visibility, connection, and acceptance within these workplaces. However, these promises of happiness remained precarious and did little for issues that mattered most (including promotion), particularly individuals of intersectionality, including ethnically diverse and female individuals.

title: Proximity vs. Pooling: Design of Parcel Locker Networks with Endogenous Service Rates
affiliations: Institute of Operations Research and Analytics, NUS,  and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management

detail.title: Proximity vs. Pooling: Design of Parcel Locker Networks with Endogenous Service Rates
detail.abstract: We study the joint location and capacity design of a spatial queueing system motivated by parcel locker operations, a widely adopted solution for last-mile delivery. Unlike classical queueing systems with exogenous service rates, locker service rates depend on customer pickup behavior and are therefore endogenous to network design. This endogeneity adds the new dimension of  "where to staff'' to the classical staffing question of  "how many to staff’’: should capacity be pooled over a fixed set of locations or distributed across an expanded network to improve customer proximity? This spatial dimension gives rise to a novel proximity–pooling trade-off. On the one hand, expanding the network improves customer proximity, shortens pickup times, and increases effective service rates, thereby reducing capacity requirements. On the other hand, network expansion fragments demand across locations, weakens risk pooling, and may increase the capacity needed to absorb demand fluctuations. Our asymptotic analysis establishes the necessity of network expansion for effectively managing the proximity–pooling trade-off. Although a fixed-location design preserves demand pooling, it sacrifices customer proximity and requires total capacity to grow linearly with the parcel arrival rate. In contrast, an appropriately expanding network balances these two forces and achieves sublinear capacity growth. For the non-asymptotic regime, we develop an optimization model and reformulate it as a mixed-integer second-order cone program. A case study based on Singapore’s parcel locker pilot program shows that the capacity-minimizing network expands as demand increases while retaining sufficient concentration to preserve pooling benefits.

title: Does Basket Assembly on HALO-Score Similarity Improve the Durability of Pairs-Trading Strategies?
affiliations: Maastricht University and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Does Basket Assembly on HALO-Score Similarity Improve the Durability of Pairs-Trading Strategies?
detail.abstract: Goldman Sachs Research's HALO framework-Heavy Assets, Low Obsolescence-argues that firms whose economic value rests on costly, slow-to-replicate physical assets are structurally insulated from technological displacement. We construct a transparent HALO score from six accounting ratios for the constituents of the STOXX Europe 600 and ask whether it carries information beyond the basket level: specifically, whether requiring the two legs of a pairs trade to have similar HALO scores makes the pair more durable. Using a monthly walk-forward pairs-trading backtest over 2021-2026, we compare an unconstrained statistical baseline against a similar-HALO book and, as a negative control, a deliberately dissimilar-HALO book. Constraining formation on the HALO gap does raise the convergence rate and lower the breakdown rate relative to baseline-but the dissimilar book, which the hypothesis predicts should be worst, improves the most. The apparent gain tracks how far each constraint thins the eligible pool under a fixed 20-pair portfolio cap, and it vanishes entirely once selection is held fixed: within the unconstrained ledger, the HALO gap predicts neither convergence nor breakdown in either period. We conclude that the HALO gap carries no usable information about pair stability, and that the observed improvement is a portfolio-construction artifact. The methodological implication generalises: any eligibility screen layered on a capped statistical ranking will appear to improve pair durability whether or not it carries economic content.

title: Multidimensional Anthropomorphism and Social Media Engagement: Field Evidence from Virtual Influencer Content
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Bocconi University and TUM School of Management,Technical University of Munich

detail.title: Multidimensional Anthropomorphism and Social Media Engagement: Field Evidence from Virtual Influencer Content
detail.abstract: Virtual influencers (VIs) give creators control over their depicted personas, including the ability to vary humanlikeness from post to post. Yet prior research typically treats anthropomorphism as a stable, unidimensional influencer-level attribute. Drawing on anthropomorphism and mindperception theory, we develop a multidimensional, post-level framework of VI anthropomorphism that distinguishes appearance, behavioral, emotional, cognitive, moral, and relational cues. Using multimodal machine learning, we measure these dimensions across 10,012 Instagram posts from 83 VIs and examine their association with social media engagement. We find that overall anthropomorphism is positively associated with engagement, but this aggregate relationship masks substantial heterogeneity. Appearance exhibits the strongest association, followed by behavioral and relational cues, while cognitive, emotional and moral cues display no reliable association with engagement. Moderation analyses indicate that expressions of thought and opinion, unrelated to engagement on average, relate positively to engagement for VIs with more female audiences and for brand-affiliated VIs, and that human-like cues exhibit stronger associations on promotional posts. We reconceptualize anthropomorphism as a controllable, multidimensional content attribute rather than a fixed property of an artificial agent and offer guidance for the strategic design of VI content.

title: Identity Pathways and Sustainable Consumer Behaviour: An Integrative Review in the Indian Context

detail.title: Identity Pathways and Sustainable Consumer Behaviour: An Integrative Review in the Indian Context
detail.abstract: This paper examines sustainable consumer behaviour (SCB) through an identity-based lens, with a focus on the Indian context. While existing SCB research highlights the role of identity in shaping pro-environmental intentions, it remains fragmented and largely grounded in high-income settings. This raises questions about how identity-based mechanisms operate in emerging markets characterised by various structural constraints. Adopting an integrative review approach, this paper synthesises literature across behavioural models, identity frameworks, and marketing perspectives. The review identifies four key identity pathways-environmental, moral, social, and consumer-and examines how they are activated and/or limited in practice. The findings suggest that while identity influences sustainability intentions, its translation into behaviour is mediated by affordability, access, and trust. This limits the predictive power of identity-based explanations when considered in isolation. The paper contributes by proposing a more integrated understanding of SCB, where identity and structural conditions jointly shape behavioural outcomes in emerging market contexts.

title: Humanity Without Borders: A Pilot Framework for Transboundary Humanitarian Governance, Local Ownership, and Accountable Protection

detail.title: Humanity Without Borders: A Pilot Framework for Transboundary Humanitarian Governance, Local Ownership, and Accountable Protection
detail.abstract: Humanitarian crises rarely respect the administrative boundaries within which they are governed, funded, and staffed. Yet governance "beyond borders" remains more of a normative hope than a working concept -- something advocates invoke but rarely define in terms that can be measured. This paper tries to close that gap. It treats transboundary humanitarian governance as a specific expression of Positive Peace, understood here as the conditions needed to prevent avoidable harm, and builds the case in three steps. First, the field would benefit from a bounded, empirically usable concept rather than another appeal to universal values. Second, that concept can be built by bringing together the cosmopolitan literature and the Capability Approach, both of which speak directly to how transboundary action reduces suffering, even though they rarely appear in the same argument. Third, a composite index can operationalize the idea across five dimensions: access to aid, capability restoration, moral-legal inclusion, institutional accountability, and long-term sustainability through localization. To show what this looks like in practice, the paper reports preliminary findings from an ongoing project comparing nine humanitarian episodes across South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East and North Africa, and Latin America. These are single-coder pilot estimates, not validated findings, and they are presented to illustrate how the index differentiates crisis settings, to surface the theoretical and practical stakes of scoring choices, and to flag where the framework still needs work. Even at this early stage, a pattern emerges: transboundary aid tracks closely with whether funding is durable, whether the response is locally owned, and whether the host state's capacity and sovereignty are being eroded by conflict or great-power rivalry. The paper closes with a graded agenda for future research -- testing coder agreement, deriving empirically grounded weights, and extending the index to more cases -- before any firmer conclusions or policy recommendations are warranted.

title: Inflation Forecasting in Pakistan: A Comparative Analysis of ARIMA and Regularized Regression Models

detail.title: Inflation Forecasting in Pakistan: A Comparative Analysis of ARIMA and Regularized Regression Models
detail.abstract: This study investigates inflation forecasting in Pakistan using annual macroeconomic data from 1980 to 2024. We employ and compare four forecasting models: ARIMA, LASSO Regression, Ridge Regression, and Elastic Net. The models are trained on data from 1980-2020 and tested on 2021-2024. Our results indicate that LASSO Regression outperforms the other models, achieving the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 30.42, followed by Elastic Net (35.52), Ridge (37.58), and ARIMA (245.37). The superior performance of LASSO is attributed to its ability to perform automatic variable selection and handle multicollinearity among economic indicators such as CPI, WPI and oil prices. This paper contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence on the effectiveness of machine learning approaches for inflation forecasting in developing economies, specifically Pakistan. The findings have important implications for policymakers and central banks in their efforts to anticipate and manage inflationary pressures.

title: A Currency for Africa: Monetary Sovereignty, Neocolonial Path-Dependence, and the Political Economy of the CFA Franc-ECO Transition

detail.title: A Currency for Africa: Monetary Sovereignty, Neocolonial Path-Dependence, and the Political Economy of the CFA Franc-ECO Transition

keywords: West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA)
Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC)

detail.abstract: The CFA franc system, established by France in 1945, still governs fourteen West and Central African states. It represents one of the longest-surviving monetary architectures inherited from formal colonial rule. This article critically reassesses the institutional design of the CFA franc zone: fixed parity, centralisation of foreign exchange reserves, and unconditional convertibility. It evaluates the extent to which these mechanisms have constrained monetary sovereignty and economic diversification in the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA) and the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC). Drawing on Optimal Currency Area theory, the article shows that neither monetary union satisfies the standard criteria for currency union viability. This is notably the case with respect to intra-regional trade integration and productive diversification. The analysis then turns to the 2019-2020 CFA-to-ECO transition. It argues that the reform announced by France and Côte d'Ivoire preserves the substantive features of the earlier arrangement-fixed euro peg and French guarantee-while removing only its most visible symbols. Finally, the article surveys alternative pan-African monetary designs. These include the single-currency ECOWAS project and the solidarity-based national currency proposals of Mamadou Igor Diarra and Samir Amin, which maintain distinct national currencies linked through shared reserve and convergence mechanisms. Both strands are situated within the broader theoretical debate on monetary sovereignty and development inaugurated by Joseph Tchundjang Pouemi. The article contributes to the political economy literature on monetary neocolonialism. It does so by systematising, within a single comparative framework, the economic, institutional and political dimensions of the CFA question.

title: Correction Factors for Electrodes of PTW Ionization Chambers in Absorbed Dose to Water Measurements for 6 MV Photon Radiotherapy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Vietnam National University Hanoi, Vietnam Atomic Energy Institute, Vietnam Atomic Energy Institute, Vietnam Atomic Energy Institute, Phenikaa University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Wollongong and Vietnam Atomic Energy Institute

detail.title: Correction Factors for Electrodes of PTW Ionization Chambers in Absorbed Dose to Water Measurements for 6 MV Photon Radiotherapy
detail.abstract: Ionization chambers (ICs) are the primary reference instruments for measuring absorbed dose to water ([[EQUATION]]) in clinical photon beams from medical linear accelerators (Linacs). However, because IC electrodes are fabricated from non-water-equivalent materials, thus investigation of perturbation correction factors for the central and outer electrodes ([[EQUATION]]) of ICs is a crucial task before applying ICs in use. This work applied PHITS code to calculate [[EQUATION]] values for 04 Freiburg PTW ICs [i.e., PTW-31021 (0.070 cm3), PTW-31010 (0.125 cm3), PTW-31013 (0.300 cm3), and PTW-30010 (0.600 cm3)]. The beam spectrum was reconstructed based on the IAEA-distributed phase-space data corresponding to a 6 MV photon beam from a Varian TrueBeam Linac. Reference conditions followed established clinical protocols: 10 cm depth in a water phantom, a 10 cm × 10 cm field size at 100 cm source-to-phantom surface distance. The [[EQUATION]] values were determined as the ratio of absorbed dose to water scored in a fully water-equivalent (dummy) geometry to that scored in a semi-realistic geometry retaining the actual electrode materials - aluminium for the central electrode and graphite-coated PMMA for the outer electrode. As results, the [[EQUATION]] values exceeded unity for all 04 chambers, ranging from 1.0003 to 1.0138, with combined statistical standard uncertainties below 1.0%. The largest correction of 1.4% was observed for the smallest-volume chamber (PTW-31021), demonstrating an inverse dependence between the magnitude of the electrode perturbation correction and the sensitive volume of the chamber. The [[EQUATION]] values are small but non-negligible, particularly for sub-0.1 cm3 ICs. The computed [[EQUATION]] values provide benchmark data applicable to both clinical and metrological dosimetry, confirming the importance of accounting for electrode material perturbations in high-accuracy absorbed dose to water measurements using ICs in clinical photon beams.

title: Syzygy: The Alignment of Personnel Reliability Systems in High-Consequence Domains

detail.title: Syzygy: The Alignment of Personnel Reliability Systems in High-Consequence Domains

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Personnel reliability systems have evolved independently across multiple high-consequence domains, including civil aviation, military service, and the management of nuclear weapons. Although developed under different legal authorities, operational requirements, and institutional cultures, these systems exhibit a remarkable convergence around a common principle: as the potential consequences of human failure increase, the rigor of personnel evaluation increases proportionally.

This monograph examines three representative institutional models within the United States: the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) medical certification system, the medical and psychological qualification standards of the U.S. Army, and the Personnel Reliability Program (PRP) governing access to nuclear weapons. Rather than comparing procedures alone, the analysis seeks to identify the underlying institutional logic shared by these apparently independent systems.

The study demonstrates that all three frameworks integrate physical health, psychological stability, behavioral reliability, and continuous evaluation according to the level of operational responsibility entrusted to the individual. The principal differences among them lie not in their fundamental philosophy, but in the degree of rigor required by the magnitude of the potential consequences associated with each role.

This convergence is described as Syzygy: the institutional alignment of independent personnel reliability systems around the common principle of proportional evaluation. The concept illustrates that proportional reliability is not a theoretical aspiration but an operational reality already implemented across multiple high-consequence domains.

Rather than proposing an entirely new certification model, this monograph argues that existing institutional practice provides empirical support for the broader frameworks developed in The Survival Blueprint. The evidence suggests that proportional personnel reliability constitutes a general principle of institutional governance capable of informing future international standards for the management of catastrophic risk.

title: The AI Competitive Advantage

detail.title: The AI Competitive Advantage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, personal, or professional relationships that could have influenced or could be perceived to have influenced this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study did not involve human participants, patient data, or the collection of personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or non-profit organization.

detail.abstract: With the prevalence of the technologies of artificial intelligence (AI) on companies ever-accelerating, such technologies have become an important matter in sustaining a competitive advantage. The strategic implications of AI on rapidly making decisions, enhancing forecasting and increasing organization resilience are discussed in this paper. The given results of the research were obtained with respect to a task-oriented and comparative analysis of the AI effects on various strategic models and examples of case studies represented with multi-sector companies, indicating that there is the potential for successful implementation of AI at the design and application stage for competitive strategies. The paper also talks about ethical concerns, digital governance and organisational culture is regarded as a barrier to AI deployment. It compares the performance of those that have deployed AI with those that haven't and the benefits, as well deficiencies. The proposed study further is useful in providing a theoretical and practical structure toward the effective application of AI technologies to re-orientate strategic processes to provide competitive advantage in volatile markets.

title: Hybrid High-Frequency Technical Trading with Order Book Information in FX Markets
affiliations: Waseda University and Waseda University - School of Political Science and Economics

detail.title: Hybrid High-Frequency Technical Trading with Order Book Information in FX Markets
detail.abstract: We examine whether limit order book information improves the profitability of high-frequency technical trading rules in FX markets. Using tick-by-tick data for EUR/USD and USD/HKD during the COVID-19 crisis and a post-crisis period, we construct one-minute hybrid strategies that combine either order-flow or order-book imbalance rules with price-based technical trading rules. Before transaction costs, hybrid rules generate higher returns with fewer trades than price-based rules and yield statistically significant profits after accounting for data-snooping bias, particularly during the crisis. Once transaction costs are included, however, the profitability of hybrid rules proves illusory. These findings show that improvements in trading signals do not necessarily translate into economic profitability after realistic execution costs.

title: Endogenous Amenities and Endogenous Markets: Evidence from Baltimore
affiliations: University of Toronto and

detail.title: Endogenous Amenities and Endogenous Markets: Evidence from Baltimore
detail.abstract: Restaurants attract residents, and residents attract restaurants.
